title.zh: 卷六十二 列傳第十二: 李綱 鄭善果 楊恭仁 皇甫無逸 李大亮
title.en: Volume 62 Biographies 12: Li Gang, Zheng Shanguo, Yang Gongren, Huangfu Wuyi, Li Daliang
title.raw: 卷六十二 列傳第十二: 李綱 鄭善果 楊恭仁 皇甫無逸 李大亮 Volume 62 Biographies 12: Li Gang, Zheng Shanguo, Yang Gongren, Huangfu Wuyi, Li Daliang

sentences.zh: 李綱，字文紀，觀州蓚人也。

translations.literal: Li Gang, style name Wenji, was a man of Zhuo in Guan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gang, whose courtesy name was Wenji, came from Zhuo in Guan Province.

sentences.zh: 祖元則，後魏清河太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yuanze was Administrator of Qinghe in Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yuanze had served as Administrator of Qinghe under the Later Wei.

sentences.zh: 父制，周車騎大將軍。

translations.literal: His father Zhi was Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhi had been Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry in the Northern Zhou.

sentences.zh: 綱少慷慨有志節，每以忠義自許。

translations.literal: Gang from youth was generous and high-spirited, ever pledging himself to loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: From his youth Gang was open-handed and high-minded, and he constantly held himself to a standard of loyalty and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 初名瑗，字子玉，讀《後漢書·張綱傳》，慕而改之。

translations.literal: His original name was Yuan, style name Ziyu; reading the biography of Zhang Gang in the Book of Later Han, he admired him and changed his name accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: He had originally been named Yuan, with the courtesy name Ziyu; after reading the biography of Zhang Gang in the Book of Later Han, he admired the man so much that he took Gang as his name.

sentences.zh: 周齊王憲引為參軍。

translations.literal: Prince Xian of Qi of Zhou summoned him as a staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi, Xian, brought him onto his staff as an aide.

sentences.zh: 宣帝將害憲，召僚屬證成其罪，綱誓之以死，終無撓辭。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan was about to harm Xian, he summoned the staff to testify to his crimes; Gang swore he would die rather than yield, and in the end never wavered in word.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan was preparing to destroy Xian, he called in the prince's staff to confirm his guilt; Gang vowed he would die before he would bend, and to the end never softened his testimony.

sentences.zh: 及憲遇害，露車載屍而出，故吏皆散，唯綱撫棺號慟，躬自埋瘞，哭拜而去。

translations.literal: When Xian met his death, his corpse was carried out on an open cart and his former subordinates all scattered; only Gang embraced the coffin and wailed, personally buried and interred him, then departed weeping and bowing.
translations.idiomatic: After Xian was killed, his body was borne out on an open cart while his former retainers scattered; Gang alone clung to the coffin and cried aloud, dug the grave and buried him with his own hands, then left after weeping and bowing.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇末，為太子洗馬。

translations.literal: At the end of the Kaihuang era of Sui, he served as Groom of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Near the close of Emperor Wen's Kaihuang reign, he was appointed Groom of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 皇太子勇嘗以歲首宴宮臣，左庶子唐令則自請奏琵琶，又歌《武媚娘》之曲。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Yong once at the New Year feasted the palace officials; Left Assistant Tang Lingze volunteered to play the pipa and also sang the tune "Lady Wu Meiniang."
translations.idiomatic: On one New Year's occasion Crown Prince Yong entertained the palace staff, and his Left Assistant Tang Lingze offered to play the pipa and sing the song "Lady Wu Meiniang."

sentences.zh: 綱自勇曰：「令則身任宮卿，職當調護，乃於宴座自比倡優，進淫聲，穢視聽。

translations.literal: Gang spoke to Yong himself, saying: "Lingze holds a palace office and his duty is to nurture and protect you, yet at this feast he compares himself to a performer, presents licentious sounds, and defiles what eyes and ears should hear.
translations.idiomatic: Gang addressed Yong directly: "Lingze holds a senior post in your household and ought to guide your conduct, yet at this banquet he acts like a street entertainer, offers indecent music, and corrupts everyone present.

sentences.zh: 事若上聞，令則罪不測，豈不累於殿下？

translations.literal: If this reaches the sovereign's ears, Lingze's punishment cannot be foreseen—would it not also implicate Your Highness?
translations.idiomatic: If the emperor hears of it, Lingze's fate is unpredictable—and would not Your Highness be dragged down with him?

sentences.zh: 臣請遽正其罪。」

translations.literal: Your servant asks to punish him at once."
translations.idiomatic: I ask leave to deal with him immediately."

sentences.zh: 勇曰：「我欲為樂耳，君勿多事。」

translations.literal: Yong said: "I only want amusement—do not meddle."
translations.idiomatic: Yong replied, "I only want a little pleasure—do not make trouble."

sentences.zh: 綱趨而出。

translations.literal: Gang hurried out.
translations.idiomatic: Gang strode out at once.

sentences.zh: 及勇廢黜，文帝召東宮官屬切讓之，無敢對者。

translations.literal: When Yong was deposed, Emperor Wen summoned the Eastern Palace staff and sharply rebuked them; none dared reply.
translations.idiomatic: After Yong was removed as heir, Emperor Wen called in the Eastern Palace staff and scolded them harshly, but no one dared answer.

sentences.zh: 綱對曰：「今日之事，乃陛下之過，非太子罪也。

translations.literal: Gang replied: "Today's affair is Your Majesty's fault, not the crown prince's crime.
translations.idiomatic: Gang answered, "What has happened today is Your Majesty's failing, not the crown prince's fault.

sentences.zh: 勇器非上品，性是常人，若得賢明之士輔導之，足堪繼嗣皇業。

translations.literal: Yong's capacity is not of the highest grade and his nature is that of an ordinary man; if worthy and enlightened men guided him, he would suffice to inherit the imperial enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Yong is not gifted above the common run and his temperament is ordinary; with wise counselors at his side he could still have carried on the imperial line.

sentences.zh: 方今多士盈朝，當擇賢者居其任，奈何以絃歌鷹犬之才侍側，至令致此？

translations.literal: Now talents fill the court; the worthy ought to hold their posts—how could men fit only for lute-song, hawks, and hounds attend at his side until things came to this?
translations.idiomatic: The court today overflows with talent, and the wise should fill every post—how could companions skilled only in music, hawking, and hunting stand at his side until matters reached this pass?

sentences.zh: 乃陛下訓導不足，豈太子之罪耶！」

translations.literal: It is that Your Majesty's instruction was insufficient—how could this be the crown prince's crime!"
translations.idiomatic: The fault lies in insufficient guidance from Your Majesty—how can this be laid on the crown prince!"

sentences.zh: 辭氣凜然，左右皆為之失色。

translations.literal: His tone was stern and imposing; those beside him all turned pale.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke with such stern force that everyone present lost color.

sentences.zh: 文帝曰：「令汝在彼，豈非擇人？」

translations.literal: Emperor Wen said: "Was it not to choose men that I placed you there?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen said, "Did I not send you there precisely to choose the right men?"

sentences.zh: 綱曰：「臣在東宮，非得言者。」

translations.literal: Gang said: "Your servant in the Eastern Palace was not one who could speak freely."
translations.idiomatic: Gang replied, "In the Eastern Palace I was not free to speak my mind."

sentences.zh: 帝奇其對，擢拜尚書右丞。

translations.literal: The emperor marveled at his reply and promoted him to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was struck by his answer and promoted him to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時左僕射楊素、蘇威當朝用事，綱每固執所見，不與之同，由是二人深惡之。

translations.literal: At the time Left Vice Directors Yang Su and Su Wei held power at court; Gang always held to his own views and did not agree with them, wherefore the two deeply hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Directors Yang Su and Su Wei then dominated the court; Gang consistently stood by his own judgment and refused to go along with them, and the two came to detest him deeply.

sentences.zh: 會遣大將軍劉方誅討林邑，楊素言於文帝曰：「林邑多珍寶，自非正人不可委。」

translations.literal: It happened that Grand General Liu Fang was sent to punish Lin-yi; Yang Su said to Emperor Wen: "Lin-yi has many precious things—only an upright man may be entrusted with them."
translations.idiomatic: When Grand General Liu Fang was dispatched to campaign against Lin-yi, Yang Su told Emperor Wen, "Lin-yi is rich in treasure—only a man of integrity should be put in charge."

sentences.zh: 因言綱可任，文帝以為行軍司馬。

translations.literal: He then said Gang was fit for the task, and Emperor Wen appointed him army campaign marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He added that Gang was suitable, and the emperor named him campaign marshal on the expedition.

sentences.zh: 劉方承素之意，屈辱綱，幾至於死。

translations.literal: Liu Fang carried out Su's intent, humiliating Gang until he nearly died.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang followed Su's wishes and humiliated Gang to the point of near death.

sentences.zh: 及軍還，久不得調。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he long went without a new assignment.
translations.idiomatic: After the army came home, he went a long time without reassignment.

sentences.zh: 後拜齊王府司馬。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Military Adjutant of the Prince of Qi's household.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Military Adjutant in the household of the Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 未幾，蘇威復令綱詣南海應接林邑，久而不召。

translations.literal: Before long Su Wei again sent Gang to the Southern Sea to receive Lin-yi; he was long not summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Su Wei again ordered Gang to the southern coast to handle Lin-yi affairs, and left him there for a long time without recall.

sentences.zh: 綱後自來奏事，威復言綱擅離所職，以之屬吏。

translations.literal: Gang later came on his own to report; Wei again said Gang had left his post without leave and handed him over to the judicial officers.
translations.idiomatic: When Gang later returned on his own to present a report, Wei again accused him of abandoning his post without permission and turned him over to the magistrates.

sentences.zh: 綱見善卜者，令筮之，遇《鼎》，因謂綱曰：「公易姓之後，方可得志而為卿輔。

translations.literal: Gang met a skilled diviner and had him cast the stalks; he obtained the hexagram Ding, and the man therefore told Gang: "Only after the ruling house changes surname will you realize your ambition and become a minister at the side of power.
translations.idiomatic: Gang consulted a skilled diviner, who cast the stalks and obtained the hexagram Ding; he then told Gang, "Only after the dynasty changes its surname will you find your ambition fulfilled and serve as a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 宜早退；

translations.literal: You ought to withdraw early;
translations.idiomatic: You should withdraw soon;

sentences.zh: 不然，有折足之敗也。」

translations.literal: otherwise there will be the disaster of a broken leg."
translations.idiomatic: otherwise you will suffer the calamity of a broken leg."

sentences.zh: 尋會赦免，屏居於鄠。

translations.literal: Soon he was pardoned in a general amnesty and lived in seclusion at E.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon released in a general amnesty and withdrew to live quietly at E.

sentences.zh: 大業末，賊帥何潘仁以綱為長史。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye era, the bandit chief He Panren made Gang his chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Daye reign, the rebel leader He Panren appointed Gang his chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 義師至京城，綱來謁見。

translations.literal: When the righteous army reached the capital, Gang came to pay his respects.
translations.idiomatic: When the founding army reached the capital, Gang came to present himself.

sentences.zh: 高祖大悅，授丞相府司錄，封新昌縣公，專掌選。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu was greatly pleased, appointed him Registrar of the Chancellor's Office, enfeoffed him as Duke of Xinchang, and put him solely in charge of selection.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu was delighted, named him Registrar of the Chancellor's Office, created him Duke of Xinchang, and entrusted him exclusively with appointments.

sentences.zh: 高祖踐祚，拜禮部尚書，兼太子詹事，典選如故。

translations.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, he was appointed Minister of Rites and concurrently Steward of the Heir Apparent, with charge of selection as before.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu ascended the throne, Gang was made Minister of Rites and concurrently Steward of the Heir Apparent, continuing to oversee appointments as before.

sentences.zh: 先是，巢王元吉授并州總管，於是縱其左右攘奪百姓，宇文歆頻諫不納，乃上表曰：「王在州之日，多出微行，常共竇誕遊獵，蹂踐谷稼，放縱親暱，公行攘奪，境內獸畜，取之殆盡。

translations.literal: Earlier, Prince of Chao Yuanji was appointed Regional Commander of Bingzhou; he then let his followers seize from the people. Yuwen Xin repeatedly remonstrated but was not heeded, and submitted a memorial saying: "While the prince was in the province he often went out incognito, constantly hunting with Dou Yan, trampling grain in the fields, indulging his intimates in open plunder—within the borders game and livestock were taken nearly to exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Prince Yuanji of Chao was made Regional Commander of Bingzhou, he allowed his entourage to rob the people at will. Yuwen Xin remonstrated again and again without effect and finally submitted a memorial: "During the prince's tenure he often slipped out in disguise, hunted constantly with Dou Yan, rode down standing crops, and let his favorites plunder openly until game and livestock within the province were nearly exhausted.

sentences.zh: 當衢而射，觀人避箭以為笑樂。

translations.literal: He shot arrows in the middle of the streets and took people's dodging the arrows as his amusement.
translations.idiomatic: He would shoot down the main streets and laugh at people scrambling to dodge his arrows.

sentences.zh: 分遣左右，戲為攻戰，至相擊刺疻傷致死。

translations.literal: He sent out his followers to play at battle, until they stabbed and wounded one another to death.
translations.idiomatic: He set his men to mock battles until they stabbed one another and killed companions in sport.

sentences.zh: 夜開府門，宣淫他室。

translations.literal: At night he opened the princely residence and committed debauchery in other households.
translations.idiomatic: At night he threw open the mansion gates and forced himself on women in other houses.

sentences.zh: 百姓怨毒，各懷憤嘆。

translations.literal: The people were full of resentment, each harboring anger and sighs.
translations.idiomatic: The common people seethed with hatred, each nursing outrage and despair.

sentences.zh: 以此守城，安能自保！」

translations.literal: With such conduct to hold a city—how could he preserve himself!"
translations.idiomatic: With such a man defending a city, how could it stand!"

sentences.zh: 元吉竟坐免。

translations.literal: Yuanji was in the end removed from office on this account.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji was ultimately dismissed because of this.

sentences.zh: 又諷父老詣闕請之，尋令復職。

translations.literal: He also prompted the elders to go to court and request his return, and before long was ordered back to his post.
translations.idiomatic: He also incited local elders to petition at court for his reinstatement, and was soon restored to office.

sentences.zh: 時劉武週率五千騎至黃蛇嶺，元吉遣車騎將軍張達以步卒百人先嘗之。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Wuzhou led five thousand horsemen to Huangshe Ridge; Yuanji sent General of Chariots and Cavalry Zhang Da with a hundred foot soldiers to probe them first.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Wuzhou advanced with five thousand cavalry to Huangshe Ridge, Yuanji sent General Zhang Da with a hundred infantry to test the enemy first.

sentences.zh: 達以步卒少，固請不行。

translations.literal: Da, finding the foot soldiers too few, firmly begged not to go.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Da protested that a hundred foot soldiers were far too few and begged repeatedly to be excused.

sentences.zh: 元吉強遣之，至則盡沒於賊。

translations.literal: Yuanji forced him to go; on arrival they were all lost to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji compelled him to march anyway, and the detachment was wiped out on contact.

sentences.zh: 達憤怒，因引武周攻陷榆次，進逼并州。

translations.literal: Da in anger thereupon led Wuzhou to take Yuci and press on toward Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In fury Zhang Da then guided Wuzhou to capture Yuci and advance on Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 元吉大懼，紿其司馬劉德威曰：「卿以老弱守城，吾以強兵出戰。」

translations.literal: Yuanji was greatly afraid and deceived his Military Adjutant Liu Dewei, saying: "You hold the city with the old and weak; I will take the strong troops out to fight."
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Yuanji deceived his adjutant Liu Dewei: "You will hold the city with the aged and weak; I will lead the main force out to give battle."

sentences.zh: 因夜出兵，攜其妻孥，棄軍奔還京師，并州遂陷。

translations.literal: He then marched out by night, took his wife and children, abandoned the army and fled back to the capital, and Bingzhou fell.
translations.idiomatic: That night he slipped out with his family, abandoned the army, and fled to the capital, and Bingzhou was lost.

sentences.zh: 高祖怒甚，謂綱曰：「元吉幼小，未習時事，故遣竇誕、宇文歆輔之。

translations.literal: Gaozu was furious and said to Gang: "Yuanji is young and has not learned affairs of state, so I sent Dou Yan and Yuwen Xin to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was furious and told Gang, "Yuanji is still young and inexperienced in government, which is why I sent Dou Yan and Yuwen Xin to guide him.

sentences.zh: 強兵數萬，食支十年，起義興運之資，一朝而棄。

translations.literal: Tens of thousands of strong troops, provisions for ten years—the resources of our uprising and founding fortune—cast away in a single morning.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of seasoned troops and provisions for ten years—the very foundation of our uprising—thrown away in a single morning.

sentences.zh: 宇文歆首畫此計，我當斬之。」

translations.literal: Yuwen Xin first devised this plan—I shall execute him."
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Xin was the first to propose this scheme—I shall have him beheaded."

sentences.zh: 綱曰：「賴歆令陛下不失愛子，臣以為有功。」

translations.literal: Gang said: "Thanks to Xin Your Majesty did not lose a beloved son—your servant considers that a merit."
translations.idiomatic: Gang replied, "Thanks to Xin Your Majesty did not lose a beloved son—I call that a service."

sentences.zh: 高祖問其故，綱對曰：「罪由竇誕不能規諷，致令軍人怨憤。

translations.literal: Gaozu asked the reason; Gang replied: "The fault lies with Dou Yan's failure to admonish, which made the soldiers resentful and angry.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu asked why, Gang answered, "The blame falls on Dou Yan, who failed to counsel the prince and let the troops grow resentful and furious.

sentences.zh: 又齊王年少，肆行驕逸放縱，左右侵漁百姓，誕曾無諫止，乃隨順掩藏，以成其釁，此誕之罪。

translations.literal: Moreover the Prince of Qi was young and wantonly arrogant and indulgent; his followers preyed on the people—Yan never remonstrated but followed and concealed, completing the provocation; this is Yan's crime.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was young and ran wild in arrogance and excess while his men preyed on the people; Yan never checked him but went along and covered things up until disaster ripened—that is Yan's guilt.

sentences.zh: 宇文歆論情則疏，向彼又淺，王之過失，悉以聞奏。

translations.literal: Yuwen Xin by affection was distant and toward him shallow in ties, yet the prince's faults he reported entirely to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Xin was not close to the prince by family ties, yet he reported every one of the prince's faults to the throne.

sentences.zh: 且父子之際，人所難言，歆言之，豈非忠懇？

translations.literal: Moreover between father and son there are things men find hard to speak—Xin spoke them; was that not loyal sincerity?
translations.idiomatic: Between father and son there are truths men shrink from speaking—Xin spoke them anyway; was that not loyal candor?

sentences.zh: 今欲誅罪，不錄其心，臣愚竊以為過。」

translations.literal: Now to punish and kill without recording his intent—your servant in his folly considers that a fault."
translations.idiomatic: To execute him now without weighing his intent seems to me a mistake."

sentences.zh: 翌日，高祖召綱入，升御坐謂曰：「今我有公，遂使刑罰不濫。

translations.literal: The next day Gaozu summoned Gang in, ascended the imperial seat and said: "Now that I have you, punishments are not abused.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Gaozu called Gang in, took his seat on the throne, and said, "With you at my side, punishments are no longer reckless.

sentences.zh: 元吉自惡，結怨於人。

translations.literal: Yuanji by his own wickedness made enemies among men.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji brought hatred on himself through his own conduct.

sentences.zh: 歆既曾以表聞，誕亦焉能制禁？」

translations.literal: Xin had already reported by memorial—how could Yan restrain and forbid?"
translations.idiomatic: Xin had already laid the facts before you in memorials—how could Yan have restrained him?"

sentences.zh: 時高祖拜舞人安叱奴為散騎常侍，綱上疏諫曰：「謹案《周禮》，均工、樂胥不得預於仕伍。

translations.literal: At the time Gaozu appointed the dancer An Chinu as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry; Gang submitted a memorial remonstrating: "According to the Rites of Zhou, the directors of craftsmen and music masters may not enter the ranks of office.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu promoted the dancer An Chinu to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Gang submitted a memorial of protest: "The Rites of Zhou bar directors of craftsmen and masters of music from the official ranks altogether.

sentences.zh: 雖復才如子野，妙等師襄，皆身終子繼，不易其業。

translations.literal: Even if talent matched Ziye or skill equaled Master Xiang, they served to the end of life and sons succeeded them, never changing their craft.
translations.idiomatic: Even men gifted as Ziye or skilled as Master Xiang spent their lives in the craft and passed it to their sons, never leaving their station.

sentences.zh: 故魏武使祢衡擊鼓，衡先解朝服，露體而擊之，雲不敢以先王法服為伶人之衣。

translations.literal: Therefore Emperor Wu of Wei had Mi Heng beat the drum; Heng first removed court robes and struck it with body bared, saying he dared not use the ritual garments of former kings as a performer's dress.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Cao Cao ordered Mi Heng to beat the drum, Heng stripped off his court robes and struck it bare-bodied, declaring he would not wear the ritual garb of former kings as a entertainer's costume.

sentences.zh: 雖齊高緯封曹妙達為王，授安馬駒為開府，既招物議，大絜彝倫，有國有家者以為殷鑑。

translations.literal: Though Qi Gaowei enfeoffed Cao Miaoda as king and gave An Maju the title of Opening the Government, they already drew public criticism and greatly disturbed the great norms—those with state and family take this as a mirror of warning.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Qi Gaowei made Cao Miaoda a king and gave An Maju an opening-government commission, the court drew public scorn and violated the great norms of governance—every ruler who holds a realm takes that as a warning.

sentences.zh: 方今新定天下，開太平之基。

translations.literal: Now the realm is newly settled and the foundation of great peace is being laid.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has only just pacified the realm and is laying the foundation of an age of peace.

sentences.zh: 起義功臣，行賞未遍；

translations.literal: Meritorious men of the uprising have not yet all been rewarded;
translations.idiomatic: The meritorious men of the uprising have not yet all received their rewards;

sentences.zh: 高才碩學，猶滯草萊。

translations.literal: men of high talent and great learning still linger among the common fields.
translations.idiomatic: men of outstanding talent and learning still languish in obscurity.

sentences.zh: 而先令舞胡，致位五品；

translations.literal: yet you first elevate a dancing barbarian to the fifth rank;
translations.idiomatic: Yet a dancing foreigner is raised to the fifth rank;

sentences.zh: 鳴玉曳組，趨馳廊廟，顧非創業垂統貽厥子孫之道也。」

translations.literal: jade sounding and ribbons trailing, rushing through halls and temples—this is surely not the way to found an enterprise, hand down the norm, and bequeath it to one's sons and grandsons."
translations.idiomatic: with jade pendants chiming and official ribbons trailing as he hurries through the halls of state—surely this is not how one founds a dynasty, sets a standard for posterity, and bequeaths it to one's heirs."

sentences.zh: 高祖不納。

translations.literal: Gaozu did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu did not heed the advice.

sentences.zh: 尋令參詳律令。

translations.literal: Before long he was ordered to examine the statutes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was assigned to help revise the statutes and ordinances.

sentences.zh: 綱在東宮，隱太子建成初甚禮遇。

translations.literal: Gang was in the Eastern Palace; the Hidden Heir Apparent Jiancheng at first treated him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in the Eastern Palace, Gang was at first treated with great respect by the Heir Apparent Li Jiancheng.

sentences.zh: 建成常往溫湯，綱時以疾不從。

translations.literal: Jiancheng often went to the hot springs; Gang at times did not follow because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Jiancheng often visited the hot springs, and Gang sometimes stayed behind on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 有進生魚於建成者，將召饔人作鱠。

translations.literal: Someone presented live fish to Jiancheng; he was about to summon the cook to make sashimi.
translations.idiomatic: When someone presented live fish to Jiancheng, he was about to call the kitchen staff to prepare sashimi.

sentences.zh: 時唐儉、趙元楷在座，各自讚能為鱠，建成從之，既而謂曰：「飛刀鱠鯉，調和鼎食，公實有之；

translations.literal: At the time Tang Jian and Zhao Yuankai were seated; each praised his own skill at sashimi, and Jiancheng followed them, then said: "Flying-knife carp sashimi and harmonizing the tripod's food—you gentlemen truly have these;
translations.idiomatic: Tang Jian and Zhao Yuankai were present and each boasted of his skill at sashimi; Jiancheng let them proceed, then remarked, "Flying-knife carp sashimi and seasoning the royal stew—you two truly excel at that;

sentences.zh: 至於審諭弼諧，固屬於李綱矣。」

translations.literal: as for examining and instructing, assisting and harmonizing, that surely belongs to Li Gang."
translations.idiomatic: but weighing counsel and harmonizing policy—that belongs to Li Gang alone."

sentences.zh: 於是遣使送絹二百匹以遺之。

translations.literal: He thereupon sent an envoy with two hundred bolts of silk as a gift to him.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent an envoy with two hundred bolts of silk as a gift for Gang.

sentences.zh: 建成後漸狎無行之徒，有猜忌之謀，不可諫止。

translations.literal: Jiancheng later gradually grew intimate with men of no conduct and harbored schemes of suspicion; he could not be remonstrated into stopping.
translations.idiomatic: Later Jiancheng grew close to worthless men and nursed schemes of suspicion that no remonstrance could check.

sentences.zh: 又思筮者之言，頻乞骸骨。

translations.literal: Gang also remembered the diviner's words and repeatedly begged to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Remembering the diviner's prophecy, Gang repeatedly asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 高祖漫罵之曰：「卿為潘仁長史，何乃羞為朕尚書？

translations.literal: Gaozu casually scolded him: "You were chief clerk to Pan Ren—why be ashamed to serve me as Minister?
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu chided him lightly: "You served as chief clerk to the bandit Pan Ren—why shrink from being my Minister of Rites?

sentences.zh: 且建成在東宮，遣卿輔導，何為屢致辭乎？」

translations.literal: Moreover Jiancheng is in the Eastern Palace and I sent you to guide him—why repeatedly offer resignations?"
translations.idiomatic: Besides, I posted you to the Eastern Palace to guide Jiancheng—why do you keep trying to quit?"

sentences.zh: 綱頓首陳謝曰：「潘仁，賊也，誠在殺害，每諫便止，所活極多，為其長史，故得無愧。

translations.literal: Gang bowed his head and apologized, saying: "Pan Ren was a bandit and truly intended slaughter; each time I remonstrated he stopped, and those saved were very many—serving as his chief clerk, I could therefore be without shame.
translations.idiomatic: Gang bowed low and answered, "Pan Ren was a rebel who meant to kill; each time I remonstrated he stopped, and countless lives were spared—serving as his chief clerk, I can hold my head up for that.

sentences.zh: 陛下功成業泰，頗自矜伐，臣以凡劣，才乖元凱，所言如水投石，安敢久為尚書？

translations.literal: Your Majesty's achievement is complete and the enterprise secure, yet you are rather self-congratulatory; your servant is mediocre and his talent falls short of the great ministers—what I say is like water cast on stone—how dare I long remain Minister?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's triumph is complete, yet you have grown somewhat self-satisfied; I am a mediocrity, far from the stature of your greatest ministers, and my words fall like water on stone—how could I dare remain Minister for long?

sentences.zh: 兼以愚臣事太子，所懷鄙見，復不探納，既無補益，所以請退。」

translations.literal: Moreover this foolish servant serves the crown prince; the humble views he holds are again not taken up—since there is no benefit, he therefore asks to withdraw."
translations.idiomatic: Serving the crown prince, my humble counsel is never heeded; I can do no good there, and that is why I ask to step down."

sentences.zh: 高祖謝曰：「知公直士，勉弼我兒。」

translations.literal: Gaozu apologized: "I know you are an upright man—do your best to assist my son."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu apologized in turn: "I know you for an honest man—do your utmost to guide my son."

sentences.zh: 於是擢拜太子少保，尚書、詹事並如故。

translations.literal: He thereupon promoted him to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent, with Minister and Steward posts unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He then promoted Gang to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent while keeping him Minister of Rites and Steward of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 綱又上書諫太子曰：「綱耄矣，日過時流，墳樹已拱，幸未就土，許傅聖躬，無以酬恩，請效愚直，伏願殿下詳之。

translations.literal: Gang again submitted a letter remonstrating with the crown prince: "Gang is aged; the days pass the flowing age, the trees at my grave already arch—I am fortunate not yet to lie in earth, yet allowed to nurture the sacred person, with no way to repay grace; I beg to offer my foolish candor and humbly wish Your Highness will examine it.
translations.idiomatic: Gang wrote again to counsel the crown prince: "I am old; the years outrun me, and the trees at my grave already bend—yet I am spared the earth and allowed to instruct your sacred person, with no way to repay that grace. I offer this blunt counsel and beg Your Highness to weigh it carefully.

sentences.zh: 竊見飲酒過多，誠非養生之術。

translations.literal: I have observed that drinking too much is truly not the method of nurturing life.
translations.idiomatic: I see that you drink too heavily, which is no way to preserve your health.

sentences.zh: 且凡為人子者，務於孝友，以慰君父之心，不宜聽受邪言，妄生猜忌。」

translations.literal: Moreover all who are sons must devote themselves to filial piety and brotherly harmony to comfort the hearts of lord and father; they ought not heed perverse words and rashly breed suspicion."
translations.idiomatic: Every son owes filial devotion and brotherly harmony to comfort his father the emperor; you should not heed malicious talk and let suspicion take root without cause."

sentences.zh: 建成覽書不懌，而所為如故。

translations.literal: Jiancheng read the letter displeased, yet acted as before.
translations.idiomatic: Jiancheng read it with displeasure but went on as before.

sentences.zh: 綱以數言事忤太子旨，道既不行，鬱鬱不得志。

translations.literal: Gang because he repeatedly spoke on affairs against the crown prince's intent, and his way could not be followed, was depressed and without fulfillment.
translations.idiomatic: Because Gang repeatedly spoke against the crown prince's wishes and his counsel went unheeded, he grew despondent and unfulfilled.

sentences.zh: 武德二年，以老表辭職，優詔解尚書，仍為太子少保。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wude he submitted a memorial on account of age to resign; an excellent edict released him from the Ministry post while he remained Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude year 2 he asked to retire on grounds of age; an edict graciously relieved him of the Ministry post while he remained Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 高祖以綱隋代名臣，甚加優禮，每手敕未嘗稱名，其見重如此。

translations.literal: Gaozu, because Gang was a famous minister of the Sui, treated him with great favor; in each personal edict he never used his name—such was the esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: Because Gang had been a renowned minister under the Sui, Gaozu treated him with exceptional honor, never addressing him by name in personal edicts—such was the regard in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 貞觀四年，拜太子少師。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenguan he was appointed Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan year 4 he was made Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 時綱有腳疾，不堪踐履，太宗特賜步輿，令綱乘至閣下，數引入禁中，問以政道。

translations.literal: At the time Gang had a foot ailment and could not walk; Taizong specially granted him a carrying chair and had Gang ride to below the pavilion, repeatedly summoning him into the inner palace to inquire about the way of government.
translations.idiomatic: Gang suffered from a foot ailment and could not walk; Taizong gave him a sedan chair so he could be carried to the council hall and often brought him into the inner palace to discuss statecraft.

sentences.zh: 又令輿入東宮，皇太子引上殿，親拜之。

translations.literal: He also had the chair enter the Eastern Palace; the crown prince led him up the hall and bowed to him in person.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent the chair into the Eastern Palace, where the crown prince received him in the hall and bowed to him in person.

sentences.zh: 綱於是陳君臣父子之道、問寢視膳之方，理順辭直，聽者忘倦。

translations.literal: Gang thereupon set forth the way of ruler and minister, father and son, and the methods of inquiring after rest and viewing meals—his reasoning orderly and words direct, and listeners forgot weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Gang then expounded the duties of ruler and minister, father and son, and the proper forms of filial attendance at court; his reasoning was clear and his words forthright, and those who heard him forgot fatigue.

sentences.zh: 太子每親政事，太宗必令綱及左僕射房玄齡、侍中王珪侍坐。

translations.literal: Whenever the crown prince personally attended to government affairs, Taizong always had Gang, Left Vice Director Fang Xuanling, and Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Gui sit in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the crown prince presided over government business, Taizong always ordered Gang, the Left Vice Director Fang Xuanling, and the Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Gui to sit beside him.

sentences.zh: 太子嘗商略古來君臣名教竭忠盡節之事，綱凜然曰：「托六尺之孤，寄百里之命，古人以為難，綱以為易。」

translations.literal: The crown prince once discussed ancient affairs of ruler-minister teaching and exhausting loyalty to the utmost in integrity; Gang sternly said: "Entrusting a six-foot orphan and committing the fate of a hundred li—the ancients thought it hard; Gang thinks it easy."
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince once discussed how ancient ministers had upheld loyalty and moral duty to the death, Gang said sternly, "To entrust an orphan and stake the fate of the realm upon oneself—the ancients called that hard; I call it easy."

sentences.zh: 每吐論發言，皆辭色慷慨，有不可奪之志。

translations.literal: Whenever he spoke in debate, his words and bearing were all impassioned, with a will that could not be swayed.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he spoke, his tone was impassioned and his resolve unshakable.

sentences.zh: 及遇疾，太宗遣尚書左僕射房玄齡詣宅存問，賜絹二百匹。

translations.literal: When he fell ill, Taizong sent Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Fang Xuanling to his residence to inquire after him and granted two hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill, Taizong sent the Left Vice Director Fang Xuanling to visit him at home and bestowed two hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 五年卒，年八十五。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died, aged eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of the reign, at the age of eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈開府儀同三司，謚曰貞。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Bells and the same ceremonial privileges as the Three Excellencies, with the posthumous title Upright.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Master of the Palace with ceremonial privileges equal to the Three Excellencies, and given the posthumous title Upright.

sentences.zh: 太子為之立碑。

translations.literal: The crown prince erected a stele for him.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince had a memorial stele erected for him.

sentences.zh: 初，周齊王憲女孀居孑立，綱自以齊王故吏，贍恤甚厚。

translations.literal: Earlier, a daughter of Prince Xian of Qi of Zhou lived as a widow alone; Gang, considering himself a former officer of the prince, supported and comforted her very generously.
translations.idiomatic: A daughter of Prince Xian of Zhou had been left a solitary widow; Gang, as a former retainer of the prince, supported her generously.

sentences.zh: 及綱卒，其女被髮號哭，如喪所生焉。

translations.literal: When Gang died, the daughter let down her hair and wailed, as if mourning one born to her.
translations.idiomatic: When Gang died, she let down her hair and wailed as though she had lost her own father.

sentences.zh: 孫少植

translations.literal: Grandson Shaozhi
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Shaozhi

sentences.zh: 子少植，隋武陽郡同功書佐，先綱卒。

translations.literal: His son Shaozhi was a clerical aide of equal merit in Wuyang commandery under Sui and died before Gang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shaozhi had served as a clerical aide in Wuyang commandery under the Sui and predeceased him.

sentences.zh: 少植子安仁，永徽中為太子左庶子。

translations.literal: Shaozhi's son Anren in the Yonghui era served as Left Assistant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Shaozhi's son Anren served as Left Assistant of the Heir Apparent during the Yonghui reign.

sentences.zh: 屬太子被廢，歸於陳邸，宮僚皆逃散，無敢辭送者，安仁獨涕泣拜辭而去，朝野義之。

translations.literal: When the crown prince was deposed and returned to the residence of Prince of Chen, the palace staff all fled and scattered, none daring to take leave in farewell; Anren alone wept, bowed in farewell and departed—the court and commonalty honored him for it.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was deposed and sent to the residence of the Prince of Chen, the palace staff scattered in flight and none dared bid him farewell; Anren alone wept, bowed in leave-taking, and departed, and the court and people praised his conduct.

sentences.zh: 後卒於恆州刺史。

translations.literal: He later died while serving as Inspector of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later died in office as Inspector of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 鄭善果

translations.literal: Zheng Shanguo
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Shanguo

sentences.zh: 鄭善果，鄭州滎澤人也。

translations.literal: Zheng Shanguo was a man of Xingze in Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Shanguo came from Xingze in Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖孝穆，西魏少司空、岐州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xiaomu was Junior Minister of Works of Western Wei and Inspector of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xiaomu had been Junior Minister of Works under Western Wei and Inspector of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 父誠，周大將軍、開封縣公。

translations.literal: His father Cheng was a Grand General of Zhou and Duke of Kaifeng county.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cheng had been a Grand General of Zhou and Duke of Kaifeng county.

sentences.zh: 大象初，討尉遲迥，力戰遇害。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Daxiang era he campaigned against Yuwen Jiong, fought fiercely and met his death in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Daxiang reign he campaigned against Yuwen Jiong, fought to the end, and was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 善果年九歲，以父死王事，詔令襲其官爵。

translations.literal: Shanguo was nine years old; because his father died in the king's service, an edict ordered him to inherit his offices and titles.
translations.idiomatic: Shanguo was only nine when, because his father had died in the emperor's service, an edict ordered him to inherit his father's rank and titles.

sentences.zh: 家人以其嬰孺，弗之告也，受冊悲慟，擗踴不能勝，觀者莫不為之流涕。

translations.literal: His family, because he was an infant, did not tell him; receiving the patent he grieved and wailed, beating his breast and stamping until he could not bear it, and onlookers all wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: His family, thinking him too young, had not told him the reason; when he received the patent of succession he wept in anguish, beating his breast and stamping his feet until he collapsed, and all who watched wept with him.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇初，改封武德郡公，拜沂州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Sui Kaihuang his fief was changed to Duke of Wude commandery and he was appointed Inspector of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaihuang reign his title was changed to Duke of Wude commandery and he was made Inspector of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 大業中，累轉魯郡太守。

translations.literal: During Daye he was transferred in succession to Grand Defender of Lu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye reign he rose through several posts to Grand Defender of Lu commandery.

sentences.zh: 善果篤慎，事親至孝。

translations.literal: Shanguo was earnest and cautious and served his mother with utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Shanguo was conscientious and deeply filial toward his mother.

sentences.zh: 母崔氏，賢明曉於政道，每善果理務，崔氏嘗於閣內聽之。

translations.literal: His mother, Lady Cui, was worthy and enlightened and understood the way of government; whenever Shanguo handled affairs, Lady Cui would listen from within the pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Cui, was wise and versed in government; whenever Shanguo adjudicated cases, she would listen from an inner room.

sentences.zh: 聞其剖斷合理，歸則大悅；

translations.literal: hearing his judgments reasonable, on his return she was greatly pleased;
translations.idiomatic: If she heard that his judgments were fair, she was delighted when he returned;

sentences.zh: 若處事不允，母則不與之言，善果伏於床前，終日不敢食。

translations.literal: if his handling of affairs was not fair, his mother would not speak with him; Shanguo would prostrate himself before her bed and all day dare not eat.
translations.idiomatic: if his decisions were unjust, she would not speak to him; Shanguo would kneel at her bedside and go the whole day without eating.

sentences.zh: 崔氏謂之曰：「吾非怒汝，反愧汝家耳。

translations.literal: Lady Cui said to him: "I am not angry with you—I am ashamed for your household.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Cui told him, "I am not angry with you; I am ashamed for your family.

sentences.zh: 汝先君在官清恪，未嘗問私，以身徇國，繼之以死。

translations.literal: Your late father in office was pure and scrupulous, never inquiring into private gain, gave his body for the state and followed with death.
translations.idiomatic: Your late father served with integrity, never sought private gain, gave his life for the state, and died in that service.

sentences.zh: 吾亦望汝繼父之心。

translations.literal: I also hope you will continue your father's heart.
translations.idiomatic: I hoped you would carry on your father's spirit.

sentences.zh: 自童子承襲茅土，今位至方伯，豈汝身能致之耶？

translations.literal: From childhood you inherited fief and rank; now you stand as a regional lord—could your person alone have brought this about?
translations.idiomatic: You inherited rank as a child and now hold a regional governorship—do you imagine you earned that by yourself?

sentences.zh: 安可不思此事而妄加嗔怒？

translations.literal: How can you not reflect on this and rashly add anger?
translations.idiomatic: How can you fail to reflect on that and indulge your temper?

sentences.zh: 內則墜爾家風，或亡官爵；

translations.literal: inwardly you will cast down your family's reputation, or lose office and title;
translations.idiomatic: Within the family you will destroy your house's reputation and perhaps lose your rank;

sentences.zh: 外則虧天子之法，以取罪戾。

translations.literal: outwardly you will fall short of the Son of Heaven's law and incur guilt and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: outwardly you will violate the emperor's law and invite punishment.

sentences.zh: 吾寡婦也，有慈無威，使汝不知教訓，以負清忠之業，吾死之日，亦何面以事汝先君乎！」

translations.literal: I am a widow, with kindness but no authority, so that you do not know instruction and betray the work of purity and loyalty—on the day I die, with what face shall I attend your late father!"
translations.idiomatic: I am a widow with kindness but no authority, and if you fail in discipline and betray your father's legacy of integrity, what face will I have when I meet your father in death!"

sentences.zh: 善果由此遂勵己為清吏，所在有政績，百姓懷之。

translations.literal: From this Shanguo thereupon urged himself to be an upright official; wherever he served he had administrative achievements and the people cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: From that time Shanguo resolved to be an upright official; wherever he served he left a record of good governance, and the people loved him.

sentences.zh: 及朝京師，煬帝以其居官儉約，蒞政嚴明，與武威太守樊子蓋者為天下第一，各賞物千段，黃金百兩，再遷大理卿。

translations.literal: When he came to court at the capital, Emperor Yang, because his conduct in office was frugal and his governance strict and clear, ranked him with Fan Zigai, Grand Defender of Wuwei, as first under heaven; each was rewarded with a thousand lengths of goods and a hundred taels of gold, and he was transferred again to Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When he attended court at the capital, Emperor Yang ranked him with Fan Zigai, Grand Defender of Wuwei, as the finest officials in the realm for frugal conduct and strict, clear governance; each received a thousand lengths of goods and a hundred taels of gold, and Shanguo was promoted again to Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 後突厥圍煬帝於雁門，以守禦功，拜右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Later when the Turks besieged Emperor Yang at Yanmen, for his merit in defense he was appointed Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks later besieged Emperor Yang at Yanmen, Shanguo was made Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness for his role in the defense.

sentences.zh: 從幸江都。

translations.literal: He followed the emperor to Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor to Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及弒逆，署為民部尚書，隨化及至遼城。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Huaji committed regicide, he appointed him Minister of the Household and he followed Huaji to Liaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuwen Huaji murdered the emperor, he appointed Shanguo Minister of the Household and took him to Liaocheng.

sentences.zh: 淮安王神通圍化及，善果為化及守禦督戰，為流矢所中。

translations.literal: Prince Huai'an Li Shentong besieged Huaji; Shanguo for Huaji directed defense and battle and was struck by a stray arrow.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Huai'an Li Shentong besieged Huaji, Shanguo commanded the defense on Huaji's behalf and was wounded by a stray arrow.

sentences.zh: 及神通退還，竇建德進軍克之。

translations.literal: When Shentong withdrew, Dou Jiande advanced his army and took it.
translations.idiomatic: After Shentong withdrew, Dou Jiande marched in and captured the city.

sentences.zh: 建德將王琮獲善果，誚之曰：「公隋室大臣也，自尊夫人亡後而清稱益衰，又忠臣子，奈何為弒君之賊殉命苦戰而傷痍若此？」

translations.literal: Jiande's general Wang Cong captured Shanguo and mocked him, saying: "You are a great minister of the Sui house; since your honored mother's death your reputation for purity has only declined, and you are moreover a loyal minister's son—how could you die in bitter battle for a regicide and be wounded like this?"
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jiande's general Wang Cong captured Shanguo and taunted him: "You were a great minister of the Sui, yet since your mother's death your reputation for integrity has only faded; you are the son of a loyal martyr—why die in bitter battle for a regicide and end up wounded like this?"

sentences.zh: 善果深愧赧，欲自殺，偽中書令宋正本馳往救止之。

translations.literal: Shanguo was deeply ashamed and flushed; he wished to kill himself, but the false Secretariat Director Song Zhengben galloped to save and stop him.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply ashamed, Shanguo tried to take his own life, but the bogus Secretariat Director Song Zhengben rode out and stopped him.

sentences.zh: 建德又不為之禮，乃奔相州。

translations.literal: Jiande also did not treat him with courtesy, so he fled to Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Jiande likewise failed to honor him, he fled to Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 淮安王神通送於京師，高祖遇之甚厚，拜太子左庶子，檢校內史侍郎，封滎陽郡公。

translations.literal: Prince Huai'an Shentong sent him to the capital; Gaozu received him very generously, appointed him Left Assistant of the Heir Apparent and Acting Vice Director of the Secretariat, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Xingyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Huai'an Shentong sent him to the capital, where Gaozu received him warmly, made him Left Assistant of the Heir Apparent and Acting Vice Director of the Secretariat, and created him Duke of Xingyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 善果在東宮，數進忠言，多所匡諫。

translations.literal: Shanguo in the Eastern Palace repeatedly offered loyal words and remonstrated in many matters.
translations.idiomatic: In the Eastern Palace Shanguo repeatedly offered loyal counsel and remonstrated on many matters.

sentences.zh: 未幾，檢校大理卿，兼民部尚書。

translations.literal: Before long he was Acting Minister of Justice and concurrently Minister of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Acting Minister of Justice while also serving as Minister of the Household.

sentences.zh: 正身奉法，甚有善績。

translations.literal: He rectified his person and upheld the law, with very good achievements.
translations.idiomatic: He conducted himself uprightly, enforced the law faithfully, and achieved a strong record of service.

sentences.zh: 制與裴寂等十人，每奏事及侍立，並令升殿，與從兄元璹在其數，時以為榮。

translations.literal: It was decreed that he and Pei Ji and nine others, whenever they reported affairs or stood in attendance, were all to ascend the hall; his cousin Yuanshan was among the number, and at the time this was considered an honor.
translations.idiomatic: An edict grouped him with Pei Ji and nine others who were always allowed to ascend the hall when reporting to the throne or attending the emperor; his cousin Yuanshan was among them, and contemporaries regarded it as a great honor.

sentences.zh: 尋坐事免。

translations.literal: Before long he was dismissed on account of an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon dismissed after an offense.

sentences.zh: 及山東平，持節為招撫大使，坐選舉不平除名。

translations.literal: When Shandong was pacified he bore the staff of authority as Commissioner for Pacification and Comfort; for unfair selections he was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: After Shandong was pacified he served as Commissioner for Pacification with imperial credentials, but was removed from office for biased appointments.

sentences.zh: 後歷禮部、刑部二尚書。

translations.literal: Later he served in succession as Minister of Rites and Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He later served in turn as Minister of Rites and Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，出為岐州刺史，復以公事免。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan he went out as Inspector of Qizhou and was again dismissed on account of public business.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenguan he was sent out as Inspector of Qizhou but was again dismissed for an official offense.

sentences.zh: 三年，起為江州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: In the third year he was raised up as Inspector of Jiangzhou and died.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he was recalled as Inspector of Jiangzhou and died in office.

sentences.zh: 從兄元璹

translations.literal: Cousin Yuanshan
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Yuanshan

sentences.zh: 元璹，隋岐州刺史、沛國公譯子也。

translations.literal: Yuanshan was son of Yi, Sui Inspector of Qizhou and Duke of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshan was the son of Yi, who had been Inspector of Qizhou and Duke of Pei under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 少以父功拜儀同大將軍，襲爵沛國公，累轉右武候將軍，改封莘國公。

translations.literal: In youth through his father's merit he was appointed General of the Palace with Equal Honor, inherited the title Duke of Pei, was transferred in succession to General of the Right Martial Guard, and his fief was changed to Duke of Shen.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was made General of the Palace with Equal Honor through his father's merit, inherited the dukedom of Pei, rose through several posts to General of the Right Martial Guard, and was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Shen.

sentences.zh: 大業中，出為文城郡守。

translations.literal: During Daye he went out as Defender of Wencheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye reign he was sent out as Defender of Wencheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 義師至河東，元璹以郡來降，征拜太常卿。

translations.literal: When the righteous army reached Hedong, Yuanshan surrendered the commandery and was summoned and appointed Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: When the founding army reached Hedong, Yuanshan surrendered his commandery and was summoned to court as Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 及定京城，以本官兼參旗將軍。

translations.literal: When the capital was secured, he retained his office and concurrently served as General of the Banner of Participation.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital was secured, he kept his post while also serving as General of the Banner of Participation.

sentences.zh: 元璹少在戎旅，尤明軍法，高祖常令巡諸軍，教其兵事。

translations.literal: Yuanshan from youth was in the army camps and especially understood military law; Gaozu often had him inspect the various armies and teach their military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshan had spent his youth in the army and was especially versed in military regulations; Gaozu often sent him to inspect the forces and instruct them in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 突厥始畢可汗弟乙力設代其兄為叱羅可汗，又劉武周將宋金剛與叱羅共為掎角，來寇汾、晉。

translations.literal: The younger brother of the Türk Shibi Qaghan, Yilish, replaced his elder brother as Chiluo Qaghan; moreover Liu Wuzhou's general Song Jingang and Chiluo acted as pincers together and came to raid Fen and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Yilish, younger brother of the Türk qaghan Shibi, succeeded his brother as Chiluo qaghan; Song Jingang, general of Liu Wuzhou, coordinated with Chiluo in a pincer attack on Fen and Jin.

sentences.zh: 詔元璹入蕃，諭以禍福，叱羅竟不納，乃欲總其部落，入寇太原，以為武周聲援。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yuanshan into the barbarian lands to instruct him on fortune and calamity; Chiluo in the end did not accept, and then wished to gather his tribes and invade Taiyuan as a sounding support for Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshan was ordered into the steppe to explain the consequences of war and peace; Chiluo refused to listen and prepared to rally his tribes, invade Taiyuan, and support Liu Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，叱羅遇疾，療之弗愈，其下疑元璹令人毒之，乃囚執元璹，不得歸，叱羅竟死。

translations.literal: Before long Chiluo fell ill and treatment did not cure him; his followers suspected Yuanshan had sent men to poison him, and therefore imprisoned Yuanshan so he could not return; Chiluo in the end died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Chiluo fell ill and could not be cured; his followers suspected Yuanshan of poisoning him, imprisoned him, and held him captive; Chiluo died in the end.

sentences.zh: 頡利嗣立，留元璹，每隨其牙帳，經數年。

translations.literal: Jieli succeeded to the throne, kept Yuanshan, and he followed their royal tent for several years.
translations.idiomatic: When Jieli succeeded as qaghan, he kept Yuanshan with him, and Yuanshan followed the royal camp for several years.

sentences.zh: 頡利後聞高祖遺其財物，又許結婚，始放元璹來還。

translations.literal: Jieli later heard that Gaozu had sent him goods and also promised marriage alliance, and only then released Yuanshan to return.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli later learned that Gaozu had sent him gifts and promised a marriage alliance, and only then allowed Yuanshan to return.

sentences.zh: 高祖勞之曰：「卿在虜庭，累載拘繫，蘇武弗之過也。」

translations.literal: Gaozu comforted him, saying: "You were in the barbarian court, detained for many years—Su Wu was not your superior."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu welcomed him, saying, "You were held captive in the steppe for years—your endurance was no less than Su Wu's."

sentences.zh: 拜鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of the Court for Diplomatic Reception.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Director of the Court for Diplomatic Reception.

sentences.zh: 尋而突厥又寇并州，時元璹在母喪，高祖令墨絰充使招慰。

translations.literal: Before long the Turks again raided Bingzhou; at the time Yuanshan was in mourning for his mother, but Gaozu had him wear unhemmed sackcloth and serve as envoy to summon and comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Turks raided Bingzhou again; though Yuanshan was in mourning for his mother, Gaozu ordered him to wear mourning garb without hemming and go as envoy to negotiate with them.

sentences.zh: 突厥從介休至晉州，數百里間，數騎數十萬，填映山谷。

translations.literal: The Turks from Jiexiu to Jinzhou, for several hundred li, with riders numbering in the hundreds of thousands, filled and covered the valleys.
translations.idiomatic: From Jiexiu to Jinzhou the Turks stretched for hundreds of li, hundreds of thousands of horsemen filling every valley.

sentences.zh: 及見元璹，責中國違背之事，元璹隨機應對，竟無所屈，因數突厥背誕之罪，突厥大慚，不能報。

translations.literal: When they saw Yuanshan they reproached China's breaches of faith; Yuanshan answered as occasion demanded and in the end was not bent, then enumerated the Turks' crimes of breaking faith, and the Turks were greatly ashamed and could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: When they met Yuanshan they accused China of breaking faith; he answered point by point without yielding, then listed the Turks' own breaches of treaty, leaving them deeply ashamed and unable to reply.

sentences.zh: 元璹又謂頡利曰：「漢與突厥，風俗各異，漢得突厥，既不能臣，突厥得漢，復何所用？

translations.literal: Yuanshan also said to Jieli: "Han and the Turks differ in customs; if Han obtains Turks it cannot make them subjects, and if Turks obtain Han, of what use is it again?
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshan also told Jieli, "Han and the Turks follow different ways of life; even if Han conquered the Turks it could not rule them, and if the Turks seized Han territory, what good would it do them?

sentences.zh: 且抄掠資財，皆入將士，在於可汗，一無所得。

translations.literal: Moreover the goods seized in plunder all go to officers and soldiers—for the qaghan there is nothing gained.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the spoils of raiding all go to your officers and soldiers—the qaghan himself gains nothing.

sentences.zh: 不如早收兵馬，遣使和好，國家必有重賚，幣帛皆入可汗，免為劬勞，坐受利益。

translations.literal: Better early to withdraw troops and horses, send envoys for peace—the state will surely have heavy rewards, and silks and cloths will all enter the qaghan, spared labor and toil, sitting to receive benefit.
translations.idiomatic: You would do better to withdraw your forces early, send envoys to make peace, and accept the rich gifts the court will send—all the silks and cloths would go to you, without toil, while you sat and reaped the profit.

sentences.zh: 大唐初有天下，即與可汗結為兄弟，行人往來，音問不絕。

translations.literal: When Great Tang first possessed the realm it at once with the qaghan became brothers; travelers came and went and messages never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tang first won the realm, your qaghan and ours swore brotherhood; envoys traveled back and forth without interruption.

sentences.zh: 今乃舍善取怨，違多就少，何也？」

translations.literal: Now you abandon the good and take resentment, violate the many for the few—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Why now abandon friendship for enmity and break a broad alliance for a narrow grievance?"

sentences.zh: 頡利納其言，即引還。

translations.literal: Jieli accepted his words and at once led his forces back.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli accepted his argument and withdrew at once.

sentences.zh: 太宗致書慰之曰：「知公已共可汗結和，遂使邊亭息警，爟火不然。

translations.literal: Taizong sent a letter comforting him, saying: "I know you have made peace with the qaghan, so that border posts cease their alarms and beacon fires are not lit.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong wrote to commend him: "I know you have made peace with the qaghan, so that the border posts are quiet and the beacon fires unlit.

sentences.zh: 和戎之功，豈唯魏絳，金石之錫，固當非遠。」

translations.literal: The merit of pacifying the barbarians—is it only Wei Jiang's? Rewards of metal and stone surely cannot be far."
translations.idiomatic: Your achievement in pacifying the frontier rivals that of Wei Jiang; rewards of gold and jade cannot be far off."

sentences.zh: 元璹自義寧已來，五入蕃充使，幾至於死者數矣。

translations.literal: From Yining onward Yuanshan five times entered the barbarian lands as envoy and several times came near death.
translations.idiomatic: From the Yining era onward Yuanshan had entered the steppe as envoy five times and several times nearly lost his life.

sentences.zh: 貞觀三年，又使入突厥，還奏曰：「突厥興亡，唯以羊馬為準。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenguan he was again sent into the Turks; on his return he reported: "The rise and fall of the Turks depends solely on sheep and horses as the measure.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan year 3 he was sent into the Türk lands again and reported on his return, "The fortunes of the Turks rise and fall solely with their flocks and herds.

sentences.zh: 今六畜疲羸，人皆菜色，又其牙內炊飯，化而為血。

translations.literal: Now the six domestic animals are worn and weak, the people all have the hue of vegetables, and moreover within their royal tent cooked rice turned into blood.
translations.idiomatic: Now their livestock are exhausted, the people are gaunt with hunger, and rice cooked in the royal tent turned to blood.

sentences.zh: 征祥如此，不出三年，必當覆滅。」

translations.literal: Ominous signs such as these—within three years they will surely be overthrown."
translations.idiomatic: With omens like these, they will surely fall within three years."

sentences.zh: 太宗然之。

translations.literal: Taizong agreed with this.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong agreed.

sentences.zh: 無幾，突厥果敗。

translations.literal: Before long the Turks indeed were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Turks were indeed defeated.

sentences.zh: 元璹後累轉左武候大將軍，坐事免。

translations.literal: Yuanshan later was transferred in succession to General of the Left Martial Guard and was dismissed on account of an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshan later rose to General of the Left Martial Guard but was dismissed after an offense.

sentences.zh: 尋起為宜州刺史，復封沛國公。

translations.literal: Before long he was raised up as Inspector of Yizhou and again enfeoffed as Duke of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as Inspector of Yizhou and re-created Duke of Pei.

sentences.zh: 元璹有干略，所在頗著聲譽。

translations.literal: Yuanshan had practical ability and wherever he served gained considerable reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshan was capable and earned a strong reputation wherever he served.

sentences.zh: 然其父譯事繼母失溫凊之禮，隋文帝曾賜以《孝經》；

translations.literal: Yet his father Yi in serving his stepmother failed the rites of warmth in winter and coolness in summer, and Emperor Wen of Sui once bestowed on him the Classic of Filial Piety;
translations.idiomatic: Yet his father Yi had failed in filial duty toward his stepmother, for which Emperor Wen of Sui once sent him a copy of the Classic of Filial Piety;

sentences.zh: 至元璹事親，又不以孝聞，清論鄙之。

translations.literal: as for Yuanshan in serving his kin, he was again not known for filial piety, and pure opinion despised him.
translations.idiomatic: and Yuanshan himself was not known for filial conduct toward his parents, which men of discernment held against him.

sentences.zh: 二十年卒，贈幽州刺史，謚曰簡。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he died; he was posthumously granted Inspector of Youzhou, with the posthumous title Simple.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year 20; posthumously he was made Inspector of Youzhou with the posthumous title Simple.

sentences.zh: 弟孫杲知名，則天時為天官侍郎。

translations.literal: His younger brother's grandson Gao was well known; in the time of Empress Wu he served as Vice Director of the Bureau of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother's grandson Gao became well known and served as Vice Director of the Bureau of Appointments under Empress Wu.

sentences.zh: 楊恭仁

translations.literal: Yang Gongren
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gongren

sentences.zh: 楊恭仁，本名綸，弘農華陰人，隋司空、觀王雄之長子也。

translations.literal: Yang Gongren, original name Lun, was a man of Huayin in Hongnong, eldest son of Xiong, Sui Minister of Works and Prince of Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gongren, whose original name was Lun, came from Huayin in Hongnong; he was the eldest son of Prince Xiong of Guan, who had served as Minister of Works under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 隋仁壽中，累除甘州刺史。

translations.literal: During Sui Renshou he was repeatedly removed and appointed Inspector of Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Renshou reign he was appointed Inspector of Ganzhou after several transfers.

sentences.zh: 恭仁務舉大綱，不為苛察，戎夏安之。

translations.literal: Gongren devoted himself to setting forth the great principles and did not engage in harsh scrutiny; barbarians and Chinese were at peace under him.
translations.idiomatic: Gongren focused on broad principles rather than petty scrutiny, and both Chinese and non-Chinese subjects lived in peace under his rule.

sentences.zh: 文帝謂雄曰：「恭仁在州，甚有善政，非唯朕舉得人，亦是卿義方所致也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wen said to Xiong: "Gongren in his province has very good government; not only did I choose the right man, it is also due to your righteous instruction."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen said to Xiong, "Gongren has governed his province with remarkable wisdom. I chose well—but credit belongs equally to your example at home."

sentences.zh: 大業初，轉吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye he was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Daye era he was made Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 楊玄感作亂，煬帝制恭仁率兵經略，與玄感戰於破陵，大敗之。

translations.literal: Yang Xuangan raised rebellion; Emperor Yang ordered Gongren to lead troops in military management; he fought Xuangan at Poling and routed him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, Emperor Yang ordered Gongren to take command; at Poling he routed Xuangan's forces.

sentences.zh: 玄感兄弟挺身遁走，恭仁與屈突通等追討獲之。

translations.literal: Xuangan and his brothers fled away bodily; Gongren together with Qutu Tong and others pursued, attacked, and captured them.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan and his brothers fled; Gongren, Qutu Tong, and others hunted them down and captured them.

sentences.zh: 軍旋，煬帝召入內殿，謂曰：「我聞破陵之陣，唯卿力戰，功最難比。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Emperor Yang summoned him into the inner hall and said: "I hear that in the battle at Poling, only you fought with full strength; your merit is hardest to compare.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign, Emperor Yang summoned him to the inner palace and said, "At Poling I am told you alone fought with the greatest valor—no one else's achievement comes close.

sentences.zh: 雖知卿奉法清慎，都不知勇決如此也。」

translations.literal: Although I knew you uphold the law with purity and caution, I did not at all know you were so bold and resolute."
translations.idiomatic: I knew you for your scrupulous and careful regard for law, but never imagined such courage and decisiveness."

sentences.zh: 納言蘇威曰：「仁者必有勇，固非虛也。」

translations.literal: Attendant Counselor Su Wei said: "The benevolent man must have courage—this is indeed not empty."
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Counselor Su Wei said, "The benevolent must also be brave—that old saying is no empty phrase."

sentences.zh: 時蘇威及左衛大將軍宇文述、御史大夫裴蘊、黃門侍郎裴矩等皆受詔參掌選事，多納賄賂，士流嗟怨。

translations.literal: At that time Su Wei, General-in-Chief of the Left Guard Yuwen Shu, Censor-in-Chief Pei Yun, Vice Director of the Yellow Gate Pei Ju, and others all received edicts to participate in managing selection affairs; they took many bribes, and the scholar-official class sighed in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Su Wei, General-in-Chief of the Left Guard Yuwen Shu, Censor-in-Chief Pei Yun, Vice Director of the Yellow Gate Pei Ju, and others had all been ordered to help manage official appointments; they accepted bribes freely, and men of rank murmured in outrage.

sentences.zh: 恭仁獨雅正自守，不為蘊等所容，由是出為河南道大使，討捕盜賊。

translations.literal: Gongren alone maintained elegant uprightness and self-restraint; he was not tolerated by Yun and the others; hence he was sent out as Commissioner of the Henan Circuit to capture bandits and robbers.
translations.idiomatic: Gongren alone held himself to upright standards and would not go along with them; Pei Yun and his circle made no room for him, and he was sent out as Henan Circuit Commissioner to hunt down bandits.

sentences.zh: 時天下大亂，行至譙郡，為硃粲所敗，奔還江都。

translations.literal: At that time the realm was in great disorder; when he reached Qiao Commandery he was defeated by Zhu Can and fled back to Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: The empire was in turmoil; near Qiao Commandery he was defeated by Zhu Can and fled back to Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及弒逆，署吏部尚書，隨至河北，為化及守魏縣。

translations.literal: Yuwen Huaji committed regicide; he appointed him Director of the Ministry of Personnel; following him to Hebei, he defended Wei County for Huaji.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuwen Huaji murdered the emperor, he made Gongren Director of the Ministry of Personnel; Gongren followed him north to Hebei and held Wei County for Huaji.

sentences.zh: 時元寶藏據有魏郡，會行人魏徵說下寶藏，執恭仁送於京師。

translations.literal: At that time Yuan Baocang held Wei Commandery; a messenger Wei Zheng came and persuaded Baocang to submit; he seized Gongren and sent him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Baocang held Wei Commandery; when the envoy Wei Zheng persuaded Baocang to surrender, Baocang seized Gongren and sent him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 高祖甚禮遇之，拜黃門侍郎，封觀國公。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu treated him with great courtesy and honor; he was appointed Vice Director of the Yellow Gate and enfeoffed as Duke of Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu received him with high honor, made him Vice Director of the Yellow Gate, and created him Duke of Guan.

sentences.zh: 尋為涼州總管。

translations.literal: Before long he became Area Commander of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Area Commander of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 恭仁素習邊事，深悉羌胡情偽，推心馭下，人吏悅服，自蔥嶺已東，併入朝貢。

translations.literal: Gongren from of old was practiced in frontier affairs and deeply understood the sentiments and deceptions of the Qiang and Hu; he led subordinates with open heart; officials and people rejoiced and submitted; from the Onion Mountains eastward all entered to pay court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Gongren had long experience on the frontier and understood the ways of the Qiang and Hu peoples; he led his subordinates with openness and trust, winning the loyalty of officials and commoners alike; from the Pamirs eastward, all submitted tribute to the court.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遙授納言，總管如故。

translations.literal: Before long he was remotely appointed Attendant Counselor, and his area commandership remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was given the title Attendant Counselor in absentia while retaining his post as area commander.

sentences.zh: 俄而突厥頡利可汗率眾數萬奄至州境，恭仁隨方備御，多設疑兵，頡利懼而退走。

translations.literal: Suddenly the Türk qaghan Jieli led a force of tens of thousands that suddenly arrived at the border of the prefecture; Gongren according to circumstances prepared defense and set up many deceptive troops; Jieli feared and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jieli Qaghan of the Turks swept in with tens of thousands of men; Gongren readied defenses on every side and deployed many decoy forces until Jieli, unnerved, withdrew.

sentences.zh: 屬瓜州刺史賀拔威擁兵作亂，朝廷憚遠，未遑征討。

translations.literal: At that time the Inspector of Guazhou Hebawei gathered troops and raised rebellion; the court feared the distance and had no leisure to campaign and suppress.
translations.idiomatic: When Hebawei, Inspector of Guazhou, raised troops in rebellion, the court shrank from the distance and could not mount a campaign in time.

sentences.zh: 恭仁乃募驍勇，倍道兼進，賊不虞兵至之速，克其二城。

translations.literal: Gongren then recruited the fierce and brave, advanced by double stages at forced speed; the rebels did not anticipate the army's swift arrival and captured two of their cities.
translations.idiomatic: Gongren raised a force of elite troops and marched at forced speed; the rebels never expected him so soon and lost two cities to him.

sentences.zh: 恭仁悉放俘虜，賊眾感其寬惠，遂相率執威而降。

translations.literal: Gongren entirely released captives; the rebel masses were moved by his leniency and kindness and thereupon together led Wei in to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Gongren released all his prisoners; moved by his mercy, the rebels in turn seized Wei and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 久之，征拜吏部尚書，遷左衛大將軍、鼓旗將軍。

translations.literal: After a long time he was summoned and appointed Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and transferred to General-in-Chief of the Left Guard and General of Drum and Banner.
translations.idiomatic: After some years he was recalled as Director of the Ministry of Personnel and promoted to General-in-Chief of the Left Guard and General of Drum and Banner.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，拜雍州牧，加左光祿大夫，行揚州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was appointed Governor of Yongzhou, given the additional title of Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and acted as Chief Administrator of the Yangzhou Grand Area Command.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan era he became Governor of Yongzhou, was given the additional rank of Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and served as chief administrator of the Yangzhou Grand Area Command.

sentences.zh: 五年，遷洛州都督。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Area Commander of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he was transferred to Area Commander of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「洛陽要重，古難其人。

translations.literal: Taizong said: "Luoyang is strategically important and weighty; since antiquity it has been hard to find the right man.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, "Luoyang is a post of vital importance, and since antiquity it has been hard to fill.

sentences.zh: 朕之子弟多矣，恐非所任，特以委公也。」

translations.literal: My sons and younger brothers are many, yet I fear they are not equal to the task; I specially entrust it to you, sir."
translations.idiomatic: I have many sons and kinsmen, but none I trust for this duty—I appoint you especially to it."

sentences.zh: 恭仁性虛澹，必以禮度自居，謙恭下士，未嘗忤物，時人方之石慶。

translations.literal: Gongren by nature was empty and tranquil; he always took ritual norms as his standard, was modest and respectful toward scholar-officials, and never gave offense to others; people of the time compared him to Shi Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Gongren was by nature modest and retiring; he held himself to ritual propriety, treated men of learning with humility, and never gave cause for offense; contemporaries compared him to Shi Qing.

sentences.zh: 恭仁弟師道，尚桂陽公主，從侄女為巢剌王妃，弟子思敬，尚安平公主，連姻帝室，益見崇重。

translations.literal: Gongren's younger brother Shidao married Princess Guiyang; a younger brother's daughter was wife of the Prince of Chao, the Assassin; his younger brother's son Si Jing married Princess Anping; linked by marriage to the imperial house, he was even more honored and esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: Gongren's younger brother Shidao married Princess Guiyang; a niece by younger brother became consort to Prince Chao the Assassin; his nephew Si Jing married Princess Anping—with such marriages into the imperial family, the clan grew ever more honored.

sentences.zh: 後以老病乞骸骨，聽以特進歸第。

translations.literal: Later because of old age and illness he requested his bones; he was permitted to return home with the honorary rank of Special Advancement.
translations.idiomatic: He later sought retirement on grounds of age and illness and was permitted to leave office as Special Advancement and return home.

sentences.zh: 十三年卒，冊贈開府儀同三司、潭州都督，陪葬昭陵，謚曰孝。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he died; by edict he was posthumously granted Grand Master with the same magnificence as opening a separate office, third rank, and Area Commander of Tanzhou; he was buried with honor at Zhaoling; his posthumous title was Filial.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year 13 and was posthumously made Grand Master of the Office with Equipage equal to the Three Excellencies and Area Commander of Tanzhou; he was buried at Zhaoling with posthumous title Filial.

sentences.zh: 子思訓

translations.literal: His son Si Xun
translations.idiomatic: Si Xun, his son

sentences.zh: 子思訓襲爵。

translations.literal: Si Xun inherited the noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: Si Xun inherited the peerage.

sentences.zh: 顯慶中，歷右屯衛將軍。

translations.literal: During Xianqing he passed through the post of General of the Right Garrison Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianqing era he served as General of the Right Garrison Guard.

sentences.zh: 時右衛大將軍慕容寶節有愛妾，置於別宅，嘗邀思訓就之宴樂。

translations.literal: At that time General-in-Chief of the Right Guard Murong Baojie had a favorite concubine placed in a separate residence; he once invited Si Xun to go there for feasting and pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: General-in-Chief of the Right Guard Murong Baojie kept a favorite concubine in a separate house and once invited Si Xun there for a feast.

sentences.zh: 思訓深責寶節與其妻隔絕，妾等怒，密以毒藥置酒，思訓飲盡便死。

translations.literal: Si Xun deeply rebuked Baojie for separating from his wife; the concubines were angry and secretly placed poison in the wine; Si Xun drank it all and immediately died.
translations.idiomatic: Si Xun sharply reproached Baojie for estranging his wife from him; the concubines in anger secretly poisoned the wine, and Si Xun died after drinking it.

sentences.zh: 寶節坐是配嶺表。

translations.literal: Baojie because of this was sentenced to exile at the Lingnan frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Baojie was exiled to the southern frontier for this.

sentences.zh: 思訓妻又詣闕稱冤，制遣使就斬之。

translations.literal: Si Xun's wife again went to the palace gate to proclaim her grievance; by edict envoys were sent to execute Baojie on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Si Xun's widow appealed at court; an edict dispatched agents to execute Baojie on the spot.

sentences.zh: 仍改《賊盜律》，以毒藥殺人之科，更從重法。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Law on Bandits and Robbers was revised; the statute on killing by poison was again made to follow heavier penalties.
translations.idiomatic: The Law on Bandits and Robbers was then amended so that murder by poison carried heavier penalties.

sentences.zh: 思訓孫睿交，本名璬，少襲爵觀國公，尚中宗女長寧公主。

translations.literal: Si Xun's grandson Ruijiao, original name Jiao, at a young age inherited the noble rank Duke of Guan and married Princess Changning, daughter of Emperor Zhongzong.
translations.idiomatic: Si Xun's grandson Ruijiao—originally named Jiao—inherited the dukedom of Guan while young and married Emperor Zhongzong's daughter, Princess Changning.

sentences.zh: 預誅張易之有功，賜實封五百戶。

translations.literal: He participated in the execution of Zhang Yizhi with merit and was granted five hundred households of actual fief.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the killing of Zhang Yizhi and was rewarded with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 神龍中，為秘書監。

translations.literal: During Shenlong he served as Director of the Imperial Library.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenlong era he served as Director of the Imperial Library.

sentences.zh: 後被貶，卒於絳州別駕。

translations.literal: Later he was demoted and died as Vice Administrator of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later demoted and died while serving as Vice Administrator of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 恭仁弟續，頗有辭學。
