translations.literal: Gongren's younger brother Xu had considerable literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: Gongren's younger brother Xu was a man of considerable literary talent.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，為鄆州刺史。

translations.literal: During Zhenguan he served as Inspector of Yunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan era he served as Inspector of Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 續孫執柔，則天時為地官尚書，則天以外氏近屬，甚優寵之。

translations.literal: Xu's grandson Zhirou, in the time of Empress Wu, served as Director of the Bureau of Revenue; Empress Wu, because he was a close maternal relative, greatly favored and indulged him.
translations.idiomatic: Xu's grandson Zhirou served as Director of the Bureau of Revenue under Empress Wu, who favored him greatly as a close relation on her mother's side.

sentences.zh: 時武承嗣、攸寧相次知政事，則天嘗曰：「我今當宗及外家，常一人為宰相。」

translations.literal: At that time Wu Chengsi and Youning successively handled state affairs; Empress Wu once said: "From now on for the imperial clan and the maternal family, there shall always be one person as chancellor."
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Chengsi and Youning were handling government in succession, Empress Wu once said, "Henceforth I shall keep one person from the imperial house and one from my mother's kin in the chancellorship."

sentences.zh: 由是執柔同中書門下三品，尋卒。

translations.literal: Hence Zhirou was made Fellow of the Secretariat and Chancellery, third rank; before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhirou was therefore made a Fellow of the Secretariat and Chancellery at the third rank, but died soon after.

sentences.zh: 執柔子滔，開元中官至吏部侍郎、同州刺史。

translations.literal: Zhirou's son Tao, during Kaiyuan reached the offices of Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and Inspector of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhirou's son Tao rose during the Kaiyuan era to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and Inspector of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 執柔弟執一，神龍初，以誅張易之功封河東郡公，累至右金吾衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Zhirou's younger brother Zhiyi, at the beginning of Shenlong, because of merit in executing Zhang Yizhi was enfeoffed as Duke of Hedong Commandery and accumulated appointments up to General-in-Chief of the Right Golden Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhirou's younger brother Zhiyi was created Duke of Hedong for his part in killing Zhang Yizhi at the start of the Shenlong era and eventually rose to General-in-Chief of the Right Golden Guard.

sentences.zh: 少弟師道

translations.literal: Younger brother Shidao
translations.idiomatic: The youngest brother, Shidao

sentences.zh: 恭仁少弟師道，隋末自洛陽歸國，授上儀同，為備身左右。

translations.literal: Gongren's youngest brother Shidao, at the end of Sui from Luoyang returned to the realm, was granted Senior Household Companion of equal rank, and served in the personal guard.
translations.idiomatic: Gongren's youngest brother Shidao came over from Luoyang at the end of the Sui and was made Senior Household Companion, serving in the personal guard.

sentences.zh: 尋尚桂陽公主，超拜吏部侍郎，累轉太常卿，封安德郡公。

translations.literal: Before long he married Princess Guiyang, was promoted over rank to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel, successively transferred to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and enfeoffed as Duke of Ande Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He soon married Princess Guiyang, was promoted directly to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel, rose through posts to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and was created Duke of Ande.

sentences.zh: 貞觀七年，代魏徵為侍中。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhenguan he replaced Wei Zheng as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan year 7 he replaced Wei Zheng as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 性周慎謹密，未嘗漏洩內事，親友或問禁中之言，乃更對以他語。

translations.literal: By nature he was thorough, cautious, careful, and secretive; he never leaked inner-court affairs; when kin and friends sometimes asked about words of the forbidden precinct, he would answer with other talk instead.
translations.idiomatic: He was careful and discreet by nature and never divulged inner-court business; when friends asked about palace affairs, he would change the subject.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「吾少窺漢史，至孔光不言溫室之樹，每欽其餘風，所庶幾也。」

translations.literal: He once said: "In my youth I glimpsed the History of Han; when I came to Kong Guang not speaking of the trees in the warm room, each time I admired his remaining influence—this is what I hope to approach."
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "As a youth I read the History of Han and admired Kong Guang, who never breathed a word about the emperor's private chamber—that is the standard I aspire to."

sentences.zh: 師道退朝後，必引當時英俊，宴集園池，而文會之盛，當時莫比。

translations.literal: After Shidao withdrew from court he always brought together the outstanding men of the age for feasts and gatherings in gardens and ponds; the splendor of his literary assemblies had no rival in the time.
translations.idiomatic: After court Shidao always gathered the finest minds of the day for feasts in his gardens; no literary salon of the age could match his.

sentences.zh: 雅善篇什，又工草隸，酣賞之際，援筆直書，有如宿構。

translations.literal: He was by nature skilled in poems and pieces, and also adept at cursive and clerical script; at the height of tipsy appreciation he would take up the brush and write directly, as if pre-composed overnight.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at poetry and at cursive and clerical calligraphy; in the heat of convivial enjoyment he could pick up a brush and write at once, as though the work had been prepared long before.

sentences.zh: 太宗每見師道所制，必吟諷嗟賞之。

translations.literal: Whenever Taizong saw what Shidao composed, he always recited and sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Taizong read Shidao's compositions, he would recite them aloud in admiration.

sentences.zh: 十三年，轉中書令。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was transferred to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 he was made Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 太子承乾逆謀事洩，與長孫無忌、房玄齡同按其獄。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Chengqian's treasonous plot leaked out, he together with Zhangsun Wuji and Fang Xuanling jointly investigated the case.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Chengqian's conspiracy was exposed, he joined Zhangsun Wuji and Fang Xuanling in investigating the case.

sentences.zh: 師道妻前夫之子趙節與承乾通謀，師道微諷太宗，冀活之，由是獲譴，罷知機密。

translations.literal: Shidao's wife's son by her former husband, Zhao Jie, colluded in the plot with Chengqian; Shidao subtly hinted to Taizong, hoping to spare him; because of this he received reprimand and was removed from handling confidential matters.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jie, Shidao's stepson, had conspired with Chengqian; Shidao hinted obliquely to Taizong in hope of saving him and was censured, losing his role in confidential state affairs.

sentences.zh: 轉吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 師道貴家子，四海人物，未能委練，所署用多非其才，而深抑貴勢及其親黨，以避嫌疑，時論譏之。

translations.literal: Shidao was a son of a noble house; men of talent throughout the four seas—he could not thoroughly entrust and drill them; many he appointed were not their match in talent; yet he deeply suppressed noble power and their kin and partisans to avoid suspicion, and contemporary opinion mocked him.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao came from a great house and lacked broad experience with men of talent from across the realm; many of his appointments were ill-chosen, yet he went out of his way to slight the powerful and their kin to avoid suspicion—contemporaries scorned him for it.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗從容謂侍臣曰：「楊師道性行純善，自無愆過。

translations.literal: Taizong once at ease said to attendant ministers: "Yang Shidao's character and conduct are pure and good; in himself he has no fault or transgression.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong once remarked casually to his ministers, "Yang Shidao is pure in character and conduct and has no fault of his own.

sentences.zh: 而情實怯懦，未甚更事，緩急不可得力。」

translations.literal: Yet in truth he is timid and weak, has not greatly experienced affairs, and in urgency or crisis cannot be relied upon for strength."
translations.idiomatic: But he is truly timid and inexperienced, and cannot be relied on when matters grow urgent."

sentences.zh: 未幾，從征高麗，攝中書令。

translations.literal: Before long he followed the campaign against Goguryeo and acted as Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he accompanied the Goguryeo campaign as acting Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 及軍還，有毀之者，稍貶為工部尚書，尋轉太常卿。

translations.literal: When the army returned, there were those who slandered him; he was slightly demoted to Director of the Ministry of Works and before long transferred to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: After the army returned, slanderers brought him down a step to Director of the Ministry of Works, and soon afterward to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 二十一年卒，贈吏部尚書、并州都督，陪葬昭陵，賜東園秘器，並為立碑。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he died; he was posthumously granted Director of the Ministry of Personnel and Area Commander of Bingzhou; he was buried with honor at Zhaoling; he was given the secret implements of the Eastern Garden and a stele was erected for him.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year 21 and was posthumously made Director of the Ministry of Personnel and Area Commander of Bingzhou; he was buried at Zhaoling with imperial funeral gifts and a memorial stele.

sentences.zh: 子豫之，尚巢剌王女壽春縣主。

translations.literal: His son Yuzhi married the Princess of Shouchun District, daughter of the Prince of Chao the Assassin.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuzhi married the Princess of Shouchun District, daughter of Prince Chao the Assassin.

sentences.zh: 居母喪，與永嘉公主淫亂，為主婿竇奉節所擒，具五刑而殺之。

translations.literal: While in mourning for his mother, he engaged in licentious disorder with Princess Yongjia; he was seized by the princess's son-in-law Dou Fengjie and, subjected to the five punishments, was put to death.
translations.idiomatic: While mourning his mother he had an affair with Princess Yongjia; her son-in-law Dou Fengjie seized him and had him executed with the full five punishments.

sentences.zh: 師道兄子思玄，高宗時為吏部侍郎、國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Shidao's elder brother's son Si Xuan, in the time of Emperor Gaozong, served as Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and Rector of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao's nephew Si Xuan served under Emperor Gaozong as Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and Rector of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 玄弟思敬，禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Xuan's younger brother Si Jing, Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Si Jing, Xuan's younger brother, served as Director of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 師道從兄子崇敬，太子詹事。

translations.literal: Shidao's elder male cousin's son Chongjing, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao's cousin Chongjing served as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 始恭仁父雄在隋，以同姓寵貴，自武德之後，恭仁兄弟名位尤盛，則天時，又以外戚崇寵。

translations.literal: From the first, when Gongren's father Xiong was in Sui, because of the shared surname he was favored and ennobled; from Wude onward, Gongren and his brothers' names and positions were especially flourishing; in the time of Empress Wu they were again highly honored as maternal relatives.
translations.idiomatic: From the first Gongren's father Xiong had risen to favor and rank under the Sui as a clansman of the imperial house; after Wude the Gongren brothers reached still greater eminence, and under Empress Wu the clan was again elevated as maternal kin.

sentences.zh: 一家之內，駙馬三人，王妃五人，贈皇后一人，三品已上官二十餘人，遂為盛族。

translations.literal: Within one family there were three imperial sons-in-law, five imperial princesses as wives, one posthumously granted empress, and more than twenty officials of third rank and above—they thus became a great clan.
translations.idiomatic: Within a single generation the family could count three imperial sons-in-law, five princess consorts, one woman posthumously made empress, and more than twenty officials of third rank or higher—it became one of the great lineages of the age.

sentences.zh: 皇甫無逸

translations.literal: Huangfu Wuyi
translations.idiomatic: Biography of Huangfu Wuyi

sentences.zh: 皇甫無逸，字仁儉，安定烏氏人。

translations.literal: Huangfu Wuyi, style name Renjian, was a man of Wushi in Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Wuyi, courtesy name Renjian, came from Wushi in Anding.

sentences.zh: 父誕，隋并州總管府司馬。

translations.literal: His father Dan served as Vice Administrator of the Bingzhou Area Command in Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dan was Vice Administrator of the Bingzhou headquarters under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 其先安定著姓，徙居京兆萬年。

translations.literal: His ancestors were a distinguished surname of Anding and moved to reside in Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: The family was an eminent Anding clan that had moved to Wannian in the Jingzhao region.

sentences.zh: 仁壽末，漢王諒於并州起兵反，誕抗節不從，為諒所殺。

translations.literal: At the end of Renshou, Prince of Han Liang at Bingzhou raised troops in rebellion; Dan upheld integrity and would not follow and was killed by Liang.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Renshou reign, when Prince Liang of Han rebelled at Bingzhou, Dan refused to join him and was killed by Liang.

sentences.zh: 無逸時在長安，聞諒反，即同居喪之禮。

translations.literal: Wuyi was then in Chang'an; hearing of Liang's rebellion, he immediately observed the rites of mourning for a cohabiting parent.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyi was in Chang'an at the time; on hearing of Liang's rebellion he at once began mourning rites for his father.

sentences.zh: 人問其故，泣而對曰：「大人平生徇節義，既屬亂常，必無苟免。」

translations.literal: When people asked the reason, weeping he replied: "My father all his life upheld integrity and righteousness; now that rebellion has occurred, he surely cannot expect escape."
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, he wept and answered, "My father lived by loyalty and rectitude; once rebellion broke out, he could not hope to survive."

sentences.zh: 尋而凶問果至。

translations.literal: Before long news of his death indeed arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Before long word of his death arrived as he had foreseen.

sentences.zh: 在喪柴毀過禮，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: During mourning he was emaciated and ruined beyond the rites and was known for filial service to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning he wasted himself beyond what ritual required and became known for filial devotion to his mother.

sentences.zh: 煬帝以誕死節，贈柱國、弘義郡公，令無逸襲爵。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang because of Dan's death in righteousness posthumously granted him Pillar of State and Duke of Hongyi Commandery and ordered Wuyi to inherit the noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang honored Dan's martyrdom with posthumous rank as Pillar of State and Duke of Hongyi and had Wuyi inherit the title.

sentences.zh: 時五等皆廢，以其時忠義之後，特封平輿侯。

translations.literal: At that time the five ranks were all abolished; because he was the descendant of one loyal and righteous at that time, he was specially enfeoffed as Marquis of Pingyu.
translations.idiomatic: The five-tier peerage had been abolished, but as the son of a loyal martyr he was specially created Marquis of Pingyu.

sentences.zh: 拜涓陽太守，甚有能名，差品為天下第一。

translations.literal: He was appointed Prefect of Juanyang and had a great reputation for ability; in grading he was ranked first under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: As Prefect of Juanyang he earned a strong reputation for competence and was graded the best administrator in the realm.

sentences.zh: 再轉右武衛將軍，甚見親委。

translations.literal: Twice transferred, he became General of the Right Martial Guard and was greatly entrusted and relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: After two further transfers he became General of the Right Martial Guard and enjoyed the emperor's close trust.

sentences.zh: 帝幸江都，以無逸留守洛陽。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Jiangdu, Wuyi was left to guard Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor traveled to Jiangdu, Wuyi was left to hold Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 及江都之變，與段達、元文都尊立越王侗為帝。

translations.literal: When the Jiangdu incident occurred, together with Duan Da and Yuan Wendu he honored and established Prince Yue Tong as emperor.
translations.idiomatic: After the turmoil at Jiangdu he joined Duan Da and Yuan Wendu in enthroning Prince Yue Tong as emperor.

sentences.zh: 王世充作難，無逸棄老母妻子，斬關而走，追騎且至，無逸曰：「吾死而後已，終不能同爾為逆。」

translations.literal: When Wang Shichong raised trouble, Wuyi abandoned his old mother, wife, and children, cut through the pass and fled; pursuing horsemen were nearly upon him; Wuyi said: "I shall stop only when I am dead; in the end I cannot join you in rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shichong rebelled, Wuyi abandoned his aged mother, wife, and children, broke through the pass, and fled; as pursuers closed in he declared, "I would die before I joined you in treason."

sentences.zh: 因解所服金帶投之於地，曰：「以此贈卿，無為相迫。」

translations.literal: Thereupon he unfastened the gold belt he wore and threw it to the ground, saying: "I give this to you—do not press me further."
translations.idiomatic: He took off his gold belt and cast it down, saying, "Take this—do not press me further."

sentences.zh: 追騎競下馬取帶，自相爭奪，由是得免。

translations.literal: The pursuing horsemen all raced to dismount and take the belt, contending with one another, and thereby he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuers dismounted to fight over the belt and he escaped.

sentences.zh: 高祖以隋代舊臣，甚尊禮之，拜刑部尚書，封滑國公，歷陝東道行台民部尚書。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu, because he was an old minister of the Sui dynasty, treated him with great honor and courtesy; he was appointed Director of the Ministry of Justice, enfeoffed as Duke of Huaguo, and passed through the posts including Director of the Ministry of Revenue of the Eastern Shaanxi Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu treated him with great respect as a former Sui minister, made him Director of the Ministry of Justice and Duke of Huaguo, and later Director of the Ministry of Revenue of the Eastern Shaanxi Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷御史大夫。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 時益部新開，刑政未洽，長吏橫恣，贓污狼藉；

translations.literal: At that time the Yi region had newly been opened; punishments and government were not harmonized; chief officials were overbearing and unrestrained, and corruption and bribery were strewn about;
translations.idiomatic: The Yi region had only recently been incorporated; law and administration were unsettled, local leaders ruled by force, and corruption ran rampant;

sentences.zh: 令無逸持節巡撫之，承製除授。

translations.literal: Wuyi was ordered to hold the staff and tour and pacify it, and by imperial rescript make appointments and dismissals.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyi was sent with imperial credentials to inspect the region and appoint officials by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 無逸宣揚朝化，法令嚴肅，蜀中甚賴之。

translations.literal: Wuyi proclaimed and spread the court's civilizing influence; laws and edicts were strict and solemn; Shu greatly relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyi enforced the imperial law with rigor and brought order to Shu, which came to rely on him greatly.

sentences.zh: 有皇甫希仁者，見無逸專制方面，徼幸上變，云：「臣父在洛陽，無逸為母之故，陰遣臣與王世充相知。」

translations.literal: There was one Huangfu Xiren who, seeing Wuyi autocratically controlling the region, sought advantage by reporting a charge, saying: "My father was in Luoyang; because of his mother Wuyi secretly sent me to become acquainted with Wang Shichong."
translations.idiomatic: One Huangfu Xiren, seeing Wuyi wield sole power in the region, tried to turn calamity to profit by lodging a denunciation: "While my father was in Luoyang, Wuyi secretly sent me to make contact with Wang Shichong on account of his mother."

sentences.zh: 高祖審其詐，數之曰：「無逸逼於世充，棄母歸朕。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu examined and found it fraudulent; he rebuked him, saying: "Wuyi was pressed by Shichong and abandoned his mother to come to me.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu saw through the fraud and rebuked him: "Wuyi was forced by Shichong to abandon his mother and came over to me.

sentences.zh: 今之委任，異於眾人。

translations.literal: His present entrustment and appointment differ from those of the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: The trust I place in him now is unlike that I give anyone else.

sentences.zh: 其在益州，極為清正。

translations.literal: His conduct in Yizhou was extremely pure and upright.
translations.idiomatic: In his post at Yizhou he was scrupulously honest and clean-handed.

sentences.zh: 此蓋群小不耐，欲誣之也。

translations.literal: This is surely because petty men cannot bear it and wish to frame him.
translations.idiomatic: This surely comes from petty men who cannot abide him and seek to slander him falsely.

sentences.zh: 此乃離間我君臣，惑亂我視聽。」

translations.literal: This is nothing but driving a wedge between lord and minister and confusing what I see and hear."
translations.idiomatic: This is an attempt to sow discord between us and cloud my judgment."

sentences.zh: 於是斬希仁於順天門，遣給事中李公昌馳往慰諭之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xiren was beheaded at Shuntian Gate, and Attendant-in-Ordinary Li Gongchang was dispatched posthaste to comfort and instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: He then had Xiren executed at Shuntian Gate and sent Attendant-in-Ordinary Li Gongchang posthaste to reassure Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 俄而又告無逸陰與蕭銑交通者，無逸時與益州行台僕射竇璡不協，於是上表自理，又言璡罪狀。

translations.literal: Before long there was another who reported that Wuyi secretly communicated with Xiao Xian; Wuyi at the time was at odds with Dou Qin, Acting Secretary of the Yizhou Field Army, so he submitted a memorial clearing himself and also set forth Qin's offenses.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward someone again denounced Wuyi for secretly colluding with Xiao Xian. Wuyi was then on bad terms with Dou Qin, Vice Director of the Yizhou Field Army, so he submitted a memorial in his own defense and laid out Qin's crimes.

sentences.zh: 高祖覽之曰：「無逸當官執法，無所迴避，必是邪佞之徒，惡直丑正，共相構扇也。」

translations.literal: Gaozu read it and said: "Wuyi in office upholds the law and makes no evasion—this must be the work of wicked flatterers who hate the upright and abhor rectitude, all inciting one another."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu read the memorial and said: "Wuyi serves in office by enforcing the law without flinching. This must be the work of treacherous flatterers who despise honest men and stir up one another against him."

sentences.zh: 因令劉世龍、溫彥博將按其事，卒無驗而止，所告者坐斬，竇璡亦以罪黜。

translations.literal: He then ordered Liu Shilong and Wen Yanbo to investigate the matter; in the end nothing was verified and the case stopped; the accuser was put to death by sentencing, and Dou Qin was also dismissed for his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Liu Shilong and Wen Yanbo to investigate. The charges proved groundless, the accuser was executed, and Dou Qin was dismissed in disgrace.

sentences.zh: 無逸既返命，高祖勞之曰：「公立身行己，朕之所悉。

translations.literal: When Wuyi had returned on his mission, Gaozu consoled him, saying: "Your conduct and personal integrity are what I know well.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuyi returned from his assignment, Gaozu reassured him: "How you govern yourself is well known to me.

sentences.zh: 比多譖訴者，但為正直致邪佞所憎耳。」

translations.literal: Recently the many slanders against you are simply because your uprightness makes the wicked flatterers hate you."
translations.idiomatic: The recent flood of denunciations against you comes only from your integrity, which the wicked cannot abide."

sentences.zh: 尋拜民部尚書，累轉益州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Minister of the Ministry of Population and was transferred in succession to Chief Administrator of the Great Protectorate of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was made Minister of Population and eventually rose to Chief Administrator of the Yizhou Great Protectorate.

sentences.zh: 閉門自守，不通賓客，左右不得出門。

translations.literal: He shut his doors and kept to himself, receiving no guests; those at his side were not permitted to leave the house.
translations.idiomatic: He kept his doors closed and lived in seclusion, admitting no visitors, and would not even let his attendants step outside.

sentences.zh: 凡所貨易，皆往他州；

translations.literal: Whatever he traded, he went to other prefectures;
translations.idiomatic: For any purchase or sale he traveled to other prefectures,

sentences.zh: 每按部，樵採不犯於人。

translations.literal: Whenever he toured his jurisdiction, woodcutters and gatherers did not transgress against the people.
translations.idiomatic: When he toured his district, even woodcutters and foragers took care not to trespass on private land.

sentences.zh: 嘗夜宿人家，遇燈炷盡，主人將續之，無逸抽佩刀斷衣帶以為炷，其廉介如此。

translations.literal: Once he lodged overnight at a commoner's home; when the lamp wick was spent and the host was about to replenish it, Wuyi drew his belt knife, cut his sash, and used it as a wick—such was his integrity and austerity.
translations.idiomatic: Once he spent the night at a peasant's home. When the lamp burned out and the host moved to trim a new wick, Wuyi drew his knife, cut his own belt sash, and burned that instead—so scrupulous was he.

sentences.zh: 然過於審慎，所上表奏，懼有誤失，必讀之數十遍，仍令官屬再三披省；

translations.literal: Yet he was excessively cautious: memorials he submitted, fearing error, he would read several tens of times, and still have his staff examine them again and again;
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was excessively cautious. Fearing mistakes in his memorials, he would read each one dozens of times and have his staff review it repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 使者就路，又追而更審，每遣一使，輒連日不得上道。

translations.literal: When a messenger was on the road, he would recall him for further review; every time he dispatched an envoy, several days would pass before he could set out.
translations.idiomatic: Even after a courier had set out, he would summon him back for another review; each dispatch was delayed for days.

sentences.zh: 議者以此少之。

translations.literal: Critics on this account thought less of him.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators faulted him for this.

sentences.zh: 母在長安疾篤，太宗令驛召之。

translations.literal: His mother in Chang'an was gravely ill; Taizong ordered him summoned by post relay.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell gravely ill in Chang'an, Taizong sent a courier to summon him at once.

sentences.zh: 無逸性至孝，承問惶懼，不能飲食，因道病卒。

translations.literal: Wuyi by nature was supremely filial; upon receiving the inquiry he was fearful and alarmed, could neither eat nor drink, and on the road died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyi was deeply filial by nature. Distressed by the summons, he could neither eat nor drink and died of illness on the journey.

sentences.zh: 贈禮部尚書，太常考行，謚曰「孝」。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Minister of Rites; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices assessed his conduct and gave the posthumous title "Filial."
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Minister of Rites. The Court of Imperial Sacrifices reviewed his life and granted him the posthumous name Filial.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書王珪駁之曰：「無逸入蜀之初，自當扶侍老母，與之同去，申其色養，而乃留在京師，子道未足，何得為孝？」

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Wang Gui objected, saying: "When Wuyi first entered Shu, he ought himself to have supported and attended his old mother and gone together with her to fulfill his duties of nurturing in joy; yet he left her in the capital—the way of a son was insufficient; how could he be called Filial?
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Wang Gui objected: "When Wuyi first went to Shu, he should have brought his aged mother with him and cared for her there. Instead he left her in the capital. His filial conduct fell short—how could he be called Filial?"

sentences.zh: 竟謚為良。

translations.literal: In the end he was given the posthumous title "Good."
translations.idiomatic: In the end his posthumous name was changed to Good.

sentences.zh: 孫忠，開元中為衛尉卿。

translations.literal: His grandson Zhong served as Chamberlain for the Imperial Insignia in the Kaiyuan era.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Zhong became Chamberlain for the Imperial Insignia during the Kaiyuan reign.

sentences.zh: 李大亮

translations.literal: Li Daliang
translations.idiomatic: Biography of Li Daliang

sentences.zh: 李大亮，雍州涇陽人。

translations.literal: Li Daliang was a man of Jingyang in Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Li Daliang came from Jingyang in Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 後魏度支尚書琰之曾孫也。

translations.literal: He was the great-grandson of Yanzhi, Minister of Revenue of Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He was a great-grandson of Yanzhi, Minister of Revenue under the Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 其先本居隴西狄道，代為著姓。

translations.literal: His ancestors originally dwelt at Didao in Longxi; for generations they were a prominent clan.
translations.idiomatic: His family originally came from Didao in Longxi and had been a distinguished clan for generations.

sentences.zh: 祖綱，後魏南岐州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Gang was Inspector of Southern Qizhou in Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Gang had served as Inspector of Southern Qizhou under the Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 父充節，隋朔州總管、武陽公。

translations.literal: His father Chongjie was Overall Commander of Shuozhou in Sui and Duke of Wuyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chongjie had been Overall Commander of Shuozhou under the Sui and held the title Duke of Wuyang.

sentences.zh: 大亮少有文武才幹，隋末，署韓國公龐玉行軍兵曹。

translations.literal: Daliang from youth had both civil and military talent; at the end of Sui he was appointed Army Staff Officer on the campaign staff of the Duke of Han, Pang Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Daliang showed civil and military promise from youth. At the end of the Sui he served as a staff officer on Pang Yu's campaign staff.

sentences.zh: 在東都與李密戰，敗，同輩百餘人皆就死，賊帥張弼見而異之，獨釋與語，遂定交於幕下。

translations.literal: At the Eastern Capital he fought Li Mi and was defeated; more than a hundred of his companions all went to their deaths; the bandit commander Zhang Bi saw him and found him unusual, alone released him and spoke with him, and they thereafter formed a friendship under the tent.
translations.idiomatic: He fought Li Mi at the Eastern Capital and was defeated. More than a hundred of his comrades were executed, but the rebel commander Zhang Bi, struck by his bearing, spared him alone and spoke with him, and they became friends under the tent.

sentences.zh: 義兵入關，大亮自東都歸國，授土門令。

translations.literal: When the righteous army entered the Pass, Daliang returned from the Eastern Capital to submit to the new regime and was appointed Magistrate of Tumen.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel forces entered the Pass, Daliang came over from the Eastern Capital and was appointed magistrate of Tumen.

sentences.zh: 屬百姓饑荒，盜賊侵寇，大亮賣所乘馬分給貧弱，勸以墾田，歲因大稔。

translations.literal: It happened that the people were stricken by famine and bandits raided; Daliang sold the horse he rode and distributed the proceeds to the poor and weak, urging them to open land for farming, and that year there was a great harvest.
translations.idiomatic: Famine and bandit raids afflicted the district. Daliang sold his own horse and distributed the proceeds among the poor, urging them to cultivate the land, and that year the harvest was abundant.

sentences.zh: 躬捕寇盜，所擊輒平。

translations.literal: He personally pursued bandits and robbers; wherever he struck, he pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: He personally hunted down bandits, and every raid he led ended in victory.

sentences.zh: 時太宗在籓，巡撫北境，聞而嗟嘆，下書勞之，賜馬一匹、帛五十段。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Qin was on the frontier tour of the northern border; hearing of this he sighed in admiration, sent a letter of commendation, and bestowed one horse and fifty bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong, then Prince of Qin, was touring the northern frontier. Impressed by the report, he sent a letter of praise and granted Daliang a horse and fifty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 其後，胡賊寇境，大亮眾少不敵，遂單馬詣賊營，召其豪帥，諭以禍福，群胡感悟，相率請降。

translations.literal: Afterward, when barbarian bandits raided the border, Daliang's force was few and could not match them; he therefore went alone on horseback to the bandit camp, summoned their chieftains, instructed them on fortune and calamity, and the barbarians were moved to understanding and one after another requested to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when nomadic raiders invaded the district, Daliang's forces were too few to resist. He rode alone into the enemy camp, summoned the tribal leaders, and reasoned with them on the consequences of their actions until they were moved to surrender en masse.

sentences.zh: 大亮又殺所乘馬，以與之宴樂，徒步而歸。

translations.literal: Daliang again slaughtered the horse he rode and used it to feast and entertain them, then returned on foot.
translations.idiomatic: Daliang slaughtered his horse to feast the chieftains, then walked home alone.

sentences.zh: 前後降者千餘人，縣境以清。

translations.literal: In all, more than a thousand who surrendered before and after; the county territory was thereby pacified.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand tribesmen surrendered in all, and the county was pacified.

sentences.zh: 高祖大悅，超拜金州總管府司馬。

translations.literal: Gaozu was greatly pleased and specially promoted him to Army Marshal of the Jin Prefecture Overall Command.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was delighted and abruptly promoted him to army marshal of the Jinzhou command.

sentences.zh: 時王世充遣其兄子弘烈據襄陽，令大亮安撫樊、鄧，以圖進取。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Shichong sent his elder brother's son Honglie to hold Xiangyang; Daliang was ordered to pacify Fan and Deng in order to plan an advance.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong had sent his nephew Honglie to hold Xiangyang. Daliang was charged with pacifying Fan and Deng to prepare for an offensive.

sentences.zh: 大亮進兵擊之，所下十餘城。

translations.literal: Daliang advanced his troops to attack him and captured more than ten cities.
translations.idiomatic: Daliang advanced and attacked, capturing more than a dozen cities.

sentences.zh: 高祖下書勞勉，遷安州刺史。

translations.literal: Gaozu sent down a letter of commendation and encouragement and transferred him to Governor of An Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sent a letter of praise and transferred him to governor of Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 又令徇廣州巴東，行次九江，會輔公祏反，大亮以計擒公礻石將張善安。

translations.literal: He was again ordered to campaign toward Badong in Guangzhou; on the way, pausing at Jiujiang, it happened that Fu Gongshi rebelled; Daliang by stratagem captured Fu Gongshi's general Zhang Shan'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was next ordered to advance toward Badong in Guangzhou. At Jiujiang he encountered Fu Gongshi's rebellion and by stratagem captured Zhang Shan'an, one of Fu's generals.

sentences.zh: 公祏尋遣兵圍猷州，刺史左難當嬰城自守，大亮率兵進援，擊賊破之。

translations.literal: Gongshi soon sent troops to besiege You Prefecture; Governor Zuo Nandang closed the city and defended himself; Daliang led troops forward in relief, struck the bandits, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Gongshi soon besieged Youzhou. Governor Zuo Nandang held the city under siege, and Daliang marched to his relief and routed the rebels.

sentences.zh: 以功賜奴婢百人，大亮謂曰：「汝輩多衣冠子女，破亡至此，吾亦何忍以汝為賤隸乎！」

translations.literal: For his merit he was granted a hundred male and female slaves; Daliang said to them: "You are mostly children of gentry families who through ruin have come to this—how could I bear to make you lowly servants!"
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was awarded a hundred captives as slaves. Daliang told them: "Most of you are sons and daughters of good families brought low by ruin. How could I bear to keep you as bond servants?"

sentences.zh: 一皆放遣。

translations.literal: He released them all.
translations.idiomatic: He freed them all.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞而嗟異，復賜婢二十人，拜越州都督。

translations.literal: Gaozu heard of this and sighed in wonder; he again bestowed twenty maidservants and appointed him Overall Commander of Yue Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu marveled at the act and again granted him twenty maidservants, appointing him overall commander of Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，轉交州都督，封武陽縣男。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan he was transferred to Overall Commander of Jiao Prefecture and enfeoffed as Baron of Wuyang County.
translations.idiomatic: In 627 he was transferred to overall commander of Jiaozhou and enfeoffed as Baron of Wuyang.

sentences.zh: 在越州寫書百卷，及徙職，皆委之廨宇。

translations.literal: While at Yue Prefecture he copied a hundred volumes of books; when he moved to another post, he left them all in the official residence.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in Yuezhou he copied a hundred volumes of books and left them all in the yamen when he moved on.

sentences.zh: 尋召拜太府卿，出為涼州都督，以惠政聞。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned and appointed Minister of the Palace Storehouse; he went out as Overall Commander of Liang Prefecture and was known for his benevolent governance.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as Minister of the Palace Storehouse, then posted as overall commander of Liangzhou, where his humane administration became renowned.

sentences.zh: 嘗有台使到州，見有名鷹，諷大亮獻之。

translations.literal: Once an imperial envoy came to the prefecture, saw a famous hawk, and hinted that Daliang should present it.
translations.idiomatic: Once an imperial envoy visited the prefecture, saw a prized hunting hawk, and subtly suggested that Daliang offer it as tribute.

sentences.zh: 大亮密表曰：「陛下久絕畋獵，而使者求鷹。

translations.literal: Daliang secretly memorialized, saying: "Your Majesty long ago ceased hunting, yet the envoy seeks a hawk.
translations.idiomatic: Daliang sent a secret memorial: "Your Majesty long ago gave up hunting, yet this envoy asks for a hawk.

sentences.zh: 若是陛下之意，深乖昔旨；

translations.literal: If this is Your Majesty's intention, it deeply departs from your former purpose;
translations.idiomatic: If this reflects Your Majesty's wish, it contradicts your earlier resolve;

sentences.zh: 如其自擅，便是使非其人。」

translations.literal: If he acted on his own authority, then the wrong man was sent as envoy."
translations.idiomatic: If he acted on his own, then the wrong man was chosen for the mission."

sentences.zh: 太宗下之書曰：「以卿兼資文武，志懷貞確，故委籓牧，當茲重寄。

translations.literal: Taizong sent down a letter saying: "Because you combine civil and military capacity and your will is upright and firm, I entrusted you with frontier command—this heavy commission.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong replied in writing: "Because you possess both civil and military gifts and hold steadfast principles, I entrusted you with this important frontier post.

sentences.zh: 比在州鎮，聲績遠彰，念此忠勤，無忘寤寐。

translations.literal: While you have been in the prefecture and garrison, your reputation and record shine far; thinking of this loyalty and diligence, I cannot forget it waking or sleeping.
translations.idiomatic: Your reputation at your post has spread far and wide. I think of your loyalty and diligence day and night.

sentences.zh: 使遣獻鷹，遂不曲順，論今引古，遠獻直言，披露腹心，非常懇到，覽用嘉嘆，不能便已。

translations.literal: When the envoy sought the hawk's presentation, you did not comply obsequiously; citing the present you drew on the past, from afar offered straight speech, laid bare your inmost heart—extraordinarily earnest—and upon reading it I sighed in praise and could not contain myself.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy asked for the hawk, you refused to oblige. Drawing on precedent to address the present, you spoke frankly from afar with extraordinary sincerity. Reading your words, I could only marvel and applaud.

sentences.zh: 有臣若此，朕復何憂！

translations.literal: With a minister such as this, what further worry have I!
translations.idiomatic: With a minister like you, what have I to fear!

sentences.zh: 宜守此誠，終始若一。

translations.literal: You ought to keep this sincerity unchanged from first to last.
translations.idiomatic: Hold to this integrity without wavering.

sentences.zh: 古人稱一言之重，侔於千金，卿之此言，深足貴矣。

translations.literal: The ancients said one word's weight equals a thousand gold; your words here are deeply worthy.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said a single truthful word is worth a thousand gold. Your words are precious indeed.

sentences.zh: 今賜卿胡瓶一枚，雖無千鎰之重，是朕自用之物。」

translations.literal: Now I bestow on you one barbarian bottle; though it has not the weight of a thousand yi, it is something I use myself."
translations.idiomatic: I now grant you a Western bottle. Though it does not weigh a thousand yi, it is something I use with my own hands."

sentences.zh: 又賜荀悅《漢紀》一部，下書曰：「卿立志方直，竭節至公，處職當官，每副所委，方大任使，以申重寄。

translations.literal: He further bestowed one copy of Xun Yue's Annals of Han and sent a letter saying: "Your resolve is square and straight, your integrity is exhausted in utmost fairness; in office you fulfill what is entrusted—about to be greatly employed to carry out this weighty commission.
translations.idiomatic: He also granted a copy of Xun Yue's Annals of Han and wrote: "Your conduct is upright, your service utterly devoted. In every post you honor the trust placed in you. Greater tasks await to justify this heavy charge.

sentences.zh: 公事之閒，宜尋典籍。

translations.literal: In the intervals of public business, you ought to seek out the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: In spare moments from your duties, you should turn to the classics.

sentences.zh: 然此書敘致既明，論議深博，極為治之體，盡君臣之義，今以賜卿，宜加尋閱也。」

translations.literal: Yet this book's narrative is already clear and its discourse deep and broad, fully setting forth the substance of governance and exhausting the meaning of lord and minister—now given to you, you ought to study it further."
translations.idiomatic: This book narrates with clarity and argues with depth, encompassing the essentials of governance and the duties of ruler and subject. I give it to you now—study it well."

sentences.zh: 時頡利可汗敗亡，北荒諸部相率內屬。

translations.literal: At that time the Khan Jiali was defeated and destroyed; the various tribes of the northern wilderness one after another submitted inward.
translations.idiomatic: About then Jiali Khan was defeated and destroyed, and the northern tribes submitted in succession.

sentences.zh: 有大度設、拓設、泥熟特勒及七姓種落等，尚散在伊吾，以大亮為西北道安撫大使以綏之，多所降附。

translations.literal: There were Dadu She, Tuo She, Nisiu Teli, and the seven-clan tribes and others still scattered at Yiwu; Daliang was made Pacification Commissioner of the Northwest Circuit to soothe them, and many submitted and attached themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Dadu She, Tuo She, Nisiu Teli, and the seven-clan tribes remained scattered at Yiwu. Daliang was appointed Northwest Circuit Pacification Commissioner to win them over, and many tribes submitted.

sentences.zh: 朝廷愍其部眾凍餒，遣於磧石貯糧，特加賑給。

translations.literal: The court pitied their tribesmen for freezing and hunger; it ordered grain stored at Qishi and specially added relief distribution.
translations.idiomatic: The court, pitying their people for cold and hunger, ordered grain stored at Qishi and granted special relief.

sentences.zh: 大亮以為於事無益，上疏曰：

translations.literal: Daliang thought this of no benefit to affairs and submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Daliang believed this was impractical and submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞欲綏遠者，必先安近。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that those who wish to pacify the distant must first secure the near.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that to win over distant peoples one must first secure those nearby.

sentences.zh: 中國百姓，天下本根；

translations.literal: The common people of China are the root of All Under Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: The people of the heartland are the foundation of the empire;

sentences.zh: 四夷之人，猶於枝葉。

translations.literal: The peoples of the four barbarians are like branches and leaves.
translations.idiomatic: the foreign tribes are but branches and leaves.

sentences.zh: 擾於根本，以厚枝附，而求久安，未之有也。

translations.literal: To disturb the root and trunk in order to fatten branch and attachment, and yet seek long security—never has there been such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: To strain the root while nourishing the branches in hope of lasting peace has never succeeded.

sentences.zh: 自古明王，化中國以信，馭夷狄以權。

translations.literal: From antiquity enlightened kings civilized China through trust and controlled the barbarians of Yi and Di through power.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, wise rulers have governed the heartland through integrity and handled the frontier tribes through firmness.

sentences.zh: 故《春秋》云：「戎狄豺狼，不可厭也；

translations.literal: Therefore the Spring and Autumn Annals says: "The Rong and Di are wolves—one cannot grow weary of guarding against them;
translations.idiomatic: As the Spring and Autumn Annals says: "The Rong and Di are wolves that can never be satisfied;

sentences.zh: 諸夏親暱，不可棄也。」

translations.literal: the various Xia are kin and close—one cannot abandon them."
translations.idiomatic: the civilized states are kin and must not be abandoned."

sentences.zh: 自陛下君臨區宇，深根固本，人逸兵強，九州殷盛，四夷自服。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty ascended to rule the realm, deeply rooting and securing the foundation, the people are at ease and the troops strong; the Nine Provinces are abundant and flourishing, and the four barbarians submit of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty took the throne, you have strengthened the foundation at home. The people prosper and the army is strong; the realm flourishes and the frontier tribes submit willingly.

sentences.zh: 今者招致突厥，雖入提封，臣愚稍覺勞費，未悟其有益也。

translations.literal: Now in summoning the Turks, though they enter the imperial domain, this subject in his foolishness slightly perceives labor and expense and does not yet discern where the benefit lies.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in summoning the Turks into the empire, I see only cost and trouble, and cannot perceive the benefit.

sentences.zh: 然河西氓庶，積御蕃夷，州縣蕭條，戶口鮮少，加因隋亂，減耗尤多。

translations.literal: Yet the common folk of Hexi, long garrisoning against the barbarians, have prefectures and counties desolate and sparse, households few; moreover because of the Sui turmoil, losses are especially great.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Hexi have long borne the burden of frontier defense. Their prefectures are depopulated, their households few, and the Sui chaos reduced them still further.

sentences.zh: 突厥未平之前，尚不安業；

translations.literal: Before the Turks were pacified, they still could not settle to their occupations;
translations.idiomatic: Before the Turks were subdued, they could not even farm in peace;

sentences.zh: 匈奴微弱已來，始就農畝。

translations.literal: since the Xiongnu grew weak, they have only now begun to take up the plow.
translations.idiomatic: only since the Xiongnu threat faded have they begun to return to the fields.

sentences.zh: 若即勞役，恐致妨損。

translations.literal: If they are immediately put to corvée labor, I fear harm and loss will follow.
translations.idiomatic: If forced into corvée duty now, I fear further damage.

sentences.zh: 以臣愚惑，請停招慰。

translations.literal: In this subject's foolish perplexity, I ask that the summoning and soothing be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: In my humble judgment, I ask that these recruitment and relief efforts be halted.

sentences.zh: 且謂之荒服者，故臣而不內。

translations.literal: Moreover those called the distant-wild service are treated as subjects but not brought within.
translations.idiomatic: The regions called the wild domain are acknowledged as subjects but not absorbed within.

sentences.zh: 是以周室愛人攘狄，竟延七百之齡；

translations.literal: Therefore the Zhou house loved its people and repelled the Di, and in the end extended its span seven hundred years;
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou cherished its people and kept the barbarians at bay, and endured seven hundred years;

sentences.zh: 秦王輕戰事胡，四十載而遂絕。

translations.literal: the King of Qin lightly engaged in warfare against the Hu, and in forty years it was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: the First Emperor treated war with the Hu lightly, and his dynasty perished within forty years.

sentences.zh: 漢文養兵靜守，天下安豐；

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Han nourished the troops and kept quiet guard; All Under Heaven was secure and abundant;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han preserved his armies and held the frontier in peace, and the realm prospered;

sentences.zh: 孝武揚威遠略，海內虛耗。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han displayed his power in distant strategy; within the seas resources were depleted.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu projected power far abroad, and the empire was drained.

sentences.zh: 雖悔輪台，追已不及。

translations.literal: Though he repented at Luntai, pursuit was already too late.
translations.idiomatic: Though he repented at Luntai, it was too late to recover.

sentences.zh: 至於隋室，早得伊吾，兼統鄯善，既得之後，勞費日甚，虛內致外，竟損無益。

translations.literal: As for the Sui house, it early gained Yiwu and also controlled Shanshan; after gaining them, labor and expense daily grew; emptying the interior to fill the exterior, in the end there was loss without benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui, early possession of Yiwu and Shanshan brought ever-rising costs—hollowing the interior to sustain the frontier, with loss and no gain.

sentences.zh: 遠尋秦、漢，近觀隋室，動靜安危，昭然備矣。

translations.literal: Searching far back to Qin and Han and looking near at the Sui house, success and failure, security and peril, are plainly complete.
translations.idiomatic: Looking back to Qin and Han and forward to the Sui, the lessons of strength and ruin are clear enough.

sentences.zh: 伊吾雖已臣附，遠在蕃磧，人非中夏，地多沙鹵。

translations.literal: Though Yiwu has already submitted as a subject, it is far in the barbarian desert; its people are not of China; its land has much sand and salt.
translations.idiomatic: Though Yiwu has submitted, it lies deep in the barbarian wastes. Its people are not Chinese, and its soil is mostly sand and salt.

sentences.zh: 其自豎立稱籓附庸者，請羈縻受之，使居塞外，必畏威懷德，永為蕃臣，蓋行虛惠，而收實福矣。

translations.literal: Those who on their own erect titles and call themselves vassal subordinates—please accept them in loose attachment, let them dwell beyond the passes; they will surely fear authority and cherish virtue, forever remain barbarian subjects—this covers showing empty grace while reaping real blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Those who declare themselves vassals should be received under loose suzerainty and kept beyond the frontier. Once they fear our strength and honor our virtue, they will remain tributaries forever—a nominal kindness that yields real gain.

sentences.zh: 近日突厥傾國入朝，既不能俘之江淮，以變其俗；

translations.literal: Recently the Turks came to court with the whole nation; since they could not be settled in the Jiang-Huai to change their customs;
translations.idiomatic: The Turks recently submitted en masse. Since we cannot resettle them in the Jiang-Huai to change their ways,

sentences.zh: 置於內地，去京不遠，雖則寬仁之義，亦非久安之計也。

translations.literal: placing them in the interior, not far from the capital—though this is the meaning of leniency and benevolence—it is also not a plan for long security.
translations.idiomatic: keeping them in the interior near the capital, though generous in intent, is no plan for lasting peace.

sentences.zh: 每見一人初降，賜物五匹、袍一領，酋帥悉授大官，祿厚位尊，理多縻費。

translations.literal: Every time one person newly submits, he is given five bolts of goods and one robe; chieftains are all granted great offices—salaries thick, positions honored—reasonably much tying-up expense.
translations.idiomatic: Each new defector receives five bolts of cloth and a robe; chieftains are given high rank and generous stipends—all of it a heavy drain on resources.

sentences.zh: 以中國之幣帛，供積惡之凶虜，其眾益多，非中國之利也。

translations.literal: Using China's silks and cloth to supply accumulated-evil fierce barbarians—their numbers daily increase; this is not to China's benefit.
translations.idiomatic: To spend the empire's wealth feeding long-hostile barbarians only swells their numbers—to China's detriment.

sentences.zh: 太宗納其奏。

translations.literal: Taizong accepted his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong approved his memorial.

sentences.zh: 八年，為劍南道巡省大使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he served as Touring Commissioner of the Jiannan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was appointed touring commissioner of the Jiannan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 大亮激濁揚清，甚獲當時之譽。

translations.literal: Daliang stirred the muddy and lifted the clear; he greatly gained the praise of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Daliang purged corruption and uplifted the honest, winning great acclaim.

sentences.zh: 及討吐谷渾，以大亮為河東道行軍總管。

translations.literal: When campaigning against Tuyuhun, Daliang was made Campaign Commander of the Hedong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When the court campaigned against Tuyuhun, Daliang was appointed campaign commander of the Hedong Circuit.

sentences.zh: 與大總管李靖等出北路，涉青海，歷河源，遇賊於蜀渾山，接戰破之，俘其名王，虜雜畜五萬計。

translations.literal: Together with Grand General Li Jing and others he marched out on the northern route, crossed the Blue Sea, passed through the River's Source, encountered the enemy at Mount Shuhun, joined battle and defeated them, captured their famed king, and seized on the order of fifty thousand mixed livestock.
translations.idiomatic: With Grand General Li Jing and others he took the northern route across the Qinghai Sea and through the River's Source, met the enemy at Mount Shuhun, routed them in battle, captured their chief, and took some fifty thousand head of livestock.

sentences.zh: 以功進爵為公，賜物千段、奴婢一百五十人，悉遺親戚。

translations.literal: For his merit his rank was advanced to Duke; he was granted a thousand bolts of goods and a hundred and fifty slaves and maidservants, all of which he bestowed on his kin.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was raised to duke and given a thousand bolts of goods and a hundred and fifty servants, all of which he gave away to his relatives.

sentences.zh: 仍罄其家資，收葬五葉宗族無後者三十餘喪，送終之禮，一時稱盛。

translations.literal: Still he exhausted his household fortune to bury more than thirty funerals of five-generation clan members who had no descendants; the rites of final send-off were at the time acclaimed as magnificent.
translations.idiomatic: He also spent his entire fortune burying more than thirty childless kinsmen across five generations, and the funeral rites were praised at the time as unmatched in splendor.

sentences.zh: 後拜左衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed general of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 十七年，晉王為皇太子，東宮僚屬，皆盛選重臣。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, when the Prince of Jin became Crown Prince, the Eastern Palace staff were all chosen with great care from among weighty ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year the Prince of Jin was made crown prince, and the Eastern Palace staff were drawn from the most eminent ministers.

sentences.zh: 以大亮兼領太子右衛率，俄兼工部尚書，身居三職，宿衛兩宮，甚為親信。

translations.literal: Daliang was made concurrently Right Guard Leader of the Crown Prince; soon he also held concurrently the post of Minister of Works. He held three offices at once, standing night watch over both palaces, and was greatly trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Daliang was made Right Guard Leader of the crown prince and soon also Minister of Works, holding three posts at once while guarding both palaces by night—a man the emperor trusted deeply.

sentences.zh: 大亮每當宿直，必通宵假寐。

translations.literal: Whenever Daliang was on night duty, he always feigned sleep throughout the night.
translations.idiomatic: On night watch Daliang always pretended to doze the whole night through.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗勞之曰：「至公宿直，我便通夜安臥。」

translations.literal: Taizong once comforted him, saying: "With you on night watch, Your Grace, I can rest peacefully through the night.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong once told him with gratitude: "With you standing watch, I can sleep soundly all night.

sentences.zh: 其見任如此。

translations.literal: Such was the trust placed in him.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the degree of trust he enjoyed.

sentences.zh: 太宗每有巡幸，多令居守。

translations.literal: Whenever Taizong went on tour, he mostly had Daliang remain to guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Taizong traveled, he usually left Daliang behind to hold the capital.

sentences.zh: 房玄齡甚重之，每稱大亮有王陵、周勃之節，可以當大位。

translations.literal: Fang Xuanling held him in great esteem and often said Daliang had the integrity of Wang Ling and Zhou Bo and could fill the highest office.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling thought highly of him and often said Daliang had the steadfastness of Wang Ling and Zhou Bo and was fit for the highest office.

sentences.zh: 大亮雖位望通顯，而居處卑陋，衣服儉率。

translations.literal: Though Daliang's rank and repute were eminent and brilliant, his dwelling was humble and shabby and his clothing plain and simple.
translations.idiomatic: Though his rank and fame were great, Daliang lived in a humble house and dressed plainly.

sentences.zh: 至性忠謹，雖妻子不見其惰容。

translations.literal: His nature was utterly loyal and careful; even his wife and children never saw on him a slack countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Utterly loyal by nature, he never showed his wife or children a careless face.

sentences.zh: 事兄嫂有同於父母。

translations.literal: In serving his elder brother and sister-in-law he was as toward parents.
translations.idiomatic: He treated his elder brother and sister-in-law as he would his own parents.

sentences.zh: 每懷張弼之恩，而久不能得。

translations.literal: He always cherished the kindness of Zhang Bi, yet for long could not find him.
translations.idiomatic: He always remembered Zhang Bi's kindness to him, but for years could not locate him.

sentences.zh: 弼時為將作丞，自匿不言。

translations.literal: Bi was then serving as Assistant Director of Palace Construction and hid himself without revealing his whereabouts.
translations.idiomatic: Bi was then an assistant director in the Directorate of Palace Buildings and kept himself hidden, saying nothing.

sentences.zh: 大亮嘗遇諸途而識之，持弼而泣，恨相得之晚。

translations.literal: Daliang once encountered him on the road and recognized him; he clasped Bi and wept, regretting that they had found each other so late.
translations.idiomatic: Daliang once met him on the road and recognized him at once; he embraced Bi and wept, grieving that they had found each other so late.

sentences.zh: 多推家產以遺弼，弼拒而不受。

translations.literal: He repeatedly pressed household property upon Bi as a gift, but Bi refused and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He tried again and again to give Bi his family property, but Bi refused every offer.

sentences.zh: 大亮言於太宗曰：「臣有今日之榮，張弼力也。

translations.literal: Daliang said to Taizong: "Your servant's present honor is Zhang Bi's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Daliang told Taizong: "Whatever honor I enjoy today, I owe to Zhang Bi.

sentences.zh: 有官爵請回。」

translations.literal: I ask that rank and salary be transferred to him.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that any rank and stipend due me be given to him instead.

sentences.zh: 太宗遂遷弼為中郎將，俄代州都督。

translations.literal: Taizong then promoted Bi to Commandant and soon made him Governor of Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong then promoted Bi to commandant and soon appointed him governor of Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 時人皆賢大亮不背恩，而多弼不自伐也。

translations.literal: People of the time all praised Daliang for not forgetting kindness, and many admired Bi for not boasting of himself.
translations.idiomatic: People praised Daliang for never forgetting a debt of gratitude, and admired Bi all the more for never boasting of his own merit.

sentences.zh: 十八年，太宗幸洛陽，令大亮副司空玄齡居中。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, when Taizong visited Luoyang, he had Daliang assist Minister of Works Xuanling in holding the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Taizong went to Luoyang and left Daliang in the capital as deputy to Minister of Works Fang Xuanling.

sentences.zh: 尋遇疾，太宗親為調藥，馳驛賜之。

translations.literal: Soon he fell ill; Taizong personally prepared medicine for him and sent it by express courier as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: He soon fell ill, and Taizong personally mixed medicine for him and sent it by express courier.

sentences.zh: 臨終上表，請停遼東之役，又言京師宗廟所在，願深以關中為意。

translations.literal: On his deathbed he submitted a memorial asking that the Liaodong campaign be halted, and further said that since the capital held the ancestral temples, he hoped deep concern would be given to the Guanzhong region.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he submitted a memorial urging an end to the Liaodong campaign and reminding the throne that the capital housed the ancestral temples and that Guanzhong deserved the deepest care.

sentences.zh: 表成而嘆曰：「吾聞禮，男子不死婦人之手。」

translations.literal: When the memorial was finished he sighed and said: "I have heard in the rites that a man should not die in a woman's hands.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was done he sighed and said: "The rites teach that a man must not die in a woman's hands.

sentences.zh: 於是命屏婦人，言終而卒，時五十九。

translations.literal: He then ordered women to be kept away; when he had finished speaking he died, aged fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered the women withdrawn; he finished speaking and died, aged fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 死之日，家無珠玉可以為唅，唯有米五石、布三十端。

translations.literal: On the day of his death his household had no pearls or jade for the mouth-ceremony—only five shi of rice and thirty bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: When he died his household had no pearls or jade for the burial rite—only five shi of rice and thirty bolts of cloth.

sentences.zh: 親戚孤遺為大亮所鞠養，服之如父者十五人。

translations.literal: Of orphaned kin raised by Daliang, fifteen served him as a father.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen orphaned relatives he had raised mourned him as they would a father.

sentences.zh: 太宗為舉哀於別次，哭之甚慟，廢朝三日。

translations.literal: Taizong held mourning rites for him in a separate hall, wept with deep grief, and suspended court for three days.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong held mourning rites for him in a side hall, wept bitterly, and suspended court for three days.

sentences.zh: 贈兵部尚書、秦州都督，謚曰懿，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the offices of Minister of War and Governor of Qinzhou; his posthumous title was Yi, and he was buried with honor at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Minister of War and governor of Qinzhou, given the posthumous name Yi, and buried beside Taizong at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 兄子道裕，永徽中為大理卿。

translations.literal: His nephew Daoyu served as Director of the Court of Judicature and Revision in the Yonghui era.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Daoyu served as director of the Court of Judicature and Revision during the Yonghui reign.

sentences.zh: 族孫迥秀

translations.literal: Clansman-descendant Jiongxiu.
translations.idiomatic: Jiongxiu, a clansman of Daliang.

sentences.zh: 迥秀，大亮族孫也。

translations.literal: Jiongxiu was a clansman-descendant of Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiongxiu was a distant kinsman of Daliang.

sentences.zh: 祖玄明，濟州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xuanming was Governor of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xuanming had been governor of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 父義本，宣州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Yiben was Governor of Xuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yiben had been governor of Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 迥秀弱冠應英材傑出舉，拜相州參軍，累轉考功員外郎。

translations.literal: At his capping Jiongxiu responded to the Outstanding Talent examination, was appointed Staff Officer of Xiangzhou, and through successive transfers became Deputy Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty Jiongxiu passed the Outstanding Talent examination, became a staff officer in Xiangzhou, and rose through the ranks to deputy director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 則天雅愛其材，甚寵待之。

translations.literal: Empress Wu personally admired his talent and greatly favored and treated him well.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu admired his ability and treated him with great favor.

sentences.zh: 掌舉數年，遷鳳閣舍人。

translations.literal: After overseeing examinations for several years, he was promoted to Attendant of the Phoenix Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: After supervising the examinations for several years, he was promoted to attendant of the Phoenix Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 迥秀母氏庶賤而色養過人，其妻崔氏嘗叱其媵婢，母聞之不悅，迥秀即時出之。

translations.literal: Jiongxiu's mother was of low-born status yet he served her face with surpassing devotion; his wife Lady Cui once scolded her maidservants, his mother heard of it and was displeased, and Jiongxiu at once sent his wife away.
translations.idiomatic: Though Jiongxiu's mother was of humble birth, he cared for her with exceptional devotion; when his wife Lady Cui scolded a maidservant and his mother took offense, Jiongxiu immediately divorced her.

sentences.zh: 或止云：「賢室雖不避嫌疑，然過非出狀，何遽如此？」

translations.literal: Some tried to stop him, saying: "Your worthy wife, though she did not avoid suspicion, her fault was not grounds for divorce—why act so hastily?
translations.idiomatic: Some tried to dissuade him: "Your worthy wife's fault hardly warrants divorce—why act so abruptly?

sentences.zh: 迥秀曰：「娶妻本以承順顏色，顏色苟違，何敢留也？」

translations.literal: Jiongxiu said: "One takes a wife precisely to accord with and please her countenance; if her countenance is displeased, how dare I keep her?"
translations.idiomatic: Jiongxiu replied: "One marries to please one's parents; if my mother is displeased, how can I keep her?"

sentences.zh: 竟不從。

translations.literal: In the end he would not heed them.
translations.idiomatic: He would not be persuaded.

sentences.zh: 長安初，歷天官、夏官二侍郎，俄同鳳閣鸞台平章事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Chang'an era he served successively as Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and Vice Director of the Ministry of War, and soon became Joint Grand Master and Concurrently Regulator of Affairs of the Phoenix Pavilion and Luan Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Chang'an era he served as vice director of the Ministries of Personnel and War in turn, and soon became a chief minister of the Phoenix Pavilion and Luan Terrace.

sentences.zh: 則天令宮人參問其母，又嘗迎入宮中，待之甚優。

translations.literal: Empress Wu had palace women visit to inquire after his mother, and also once had her brought into the palace, treating her with great favor.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu sent palace women to inquire after his mother and once had her brought to court, treating her with exceptional kindness.

sentences.zh: 迥秀雅有文才，飲酒斗余，廣接賓朋，當時稱為風流之士。

translations.literal: Jiongxiu was naturally gifted in letters, could drink more than a dou of wine, and widely received guests and friends; of the time he was called a man of cultivated charm.
translations.idiomatic: Jiongxiu was a gifted writer who could drink more than a gallon of wine at a sitting and kept a wide circle of friends; contemporaries called him a man of refined taste.

sentences.zh: 然頗托附權幸，傾心以事張易之、昌宗兄弟，由是深為讜正之士所譏。

translations.literal: Yet he rather leaned on the powerful and favored, giving his heart devotedly to serve the brothers Zhang Yizhi and Changzong; for this he was deeply ridiculed by upright men.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he curried favor with the powerful and devoted himself to the brothers Zhang Yizhi and Changzong, earning the scorn of upright men.

sentences.zh: 俄坐贓，出為廬州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was convicted of corruption and sent out as Governor of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon convicted of corruption and demoted to governor of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 景龍中，累轉鴻臚卿、修文館學士，又持節為朔方道行軍大總管。

translations.literal: In the Jinglong era he rose through successive posts to Minister of Ceremonies and Academician of the Xiunwen Hall, and also held the staff of authority as Grand Campaign Commander of the Shuofang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jinglong era he rose to Minister of Ceremonies and academician of the Xiunwen Hall, and also served as grand campaign commander of the Shuofang Circuit with imperial authority.

sentences.zh: 所居宅中生芝草數莖，又有貓為犬所乳，中宗以為孝感所致，使旌其門閭。

translations.literal: At his residence several stalks of auspicious fungus grew, and also a cat was suckled by a dog; Zhongzong took this as caused by filial feeling and had his gate and lane honored with commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Several stalks of auspicious fungus sprang up at his house, and a cat was nursed by a dog; Emperor Zhongzong took this as a sign of filial devotion and had his gate honored with an imperial commendation.

sentences.zh: 俄代姚崇為兵部尚書，病卒。

translations.literal: Soon he replaced Yao Chong as Minister of War and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He soon succeeded Yao Chong as Minister of War and died of illness.

sentences.zh: 子齊損，開元十年，與權梁山等構逆伏誅，籍沒其家也。

translations.literal: His son Qisun, in the tenth year of Kaiyuan, joined Quan Liangshan and others in plotting rebellion and was executed; his household property was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qisun, in the tenth year of Kaiyuan, joined Quan Liangshan and others in a rebellion and was executed; the family's property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：孔子雲，「邦有道，危言危行。」

translations.literal: The Historian says: Confucius said, "When the state has the Way, one speaks dangerous words and performs dangerous deeds.
translations.idiomatic: The Historian writes: Confucius said, "When the state follows the Way, one speaks boldly and acts boldly.

sentences.zh: 如李綱直道事人，執心不回。

translations.literal: Such was Li Gang—serving men on the straight path, his heart steadfast and unyielding.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gang was such a man—serving with integrity, his heart never wavering.

sentences.zh: 始對隋文，慷慨獲免；

translations.literal: At first facing Emperor Wen of Sui, he spoke boldly and was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Before Emperor Wen of Sui he spoke boldly and was spared.

sentences.zh: 終忤楊素，屈辱尤深。

translations.literal: In the end offending Yang Su, he suffered humiliation most deeply.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he offended Yang Su and suffered deep humiliation.

sentences.zh: 及高祖臨朝，諫舞胡鳴玉，懷不吐不茹之節，存有始有卒之規，可謂危矣。

translations.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, he remonstrated against the Hu dance and the jade bells, harboring the integrity of neither spitting out nor swallowing down, keeping the design of having a beginning and an end—one might say he was in peril.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, he remonstrated against the Hu dance and jade chimes, steadfast in principle from first to last—truly a perilous course.

sentences.zh: 非逢有道，焉能免諸？

translations.literal: Had he not met a ruler who possessed the Way, how could he have escaped such things?
translations.idiomatic: Had he not served a righteous sovereign, how could he have survived?

sentences.zh: 《易》曰，「王臣蹇蹇，匪躬之故」，李綱有焉。

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says, "The king's minister, in difficulty upon difficulty—for the sake of the body, not his own"; Li Gang had this.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says, "The king's minister faces hardship after hardship—not for himself but for his sovereign"—this was Li Gang.

sentences.zh: 善果幼事賢母，長為正人。

translations.literal: Shangguo as a child served a worthy mother; grown, he became an upright man.
translations.idiomatic: Shangguo served a worthy mother in youth and grew into an upright man.

sentences.zh: 元璹於國有功，祗練邊事，承家不孝，終為匪人。

translations.literal: Yuanxu had merit for the state and was devoted to frontier affairs, yet failed in filial duty toward the family and in the end became a wicked man.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxu served the state well on the frontier, yet was unfilial at home and in the end became a villain.

sentences.zh: 恭仁仕隋忠厚，馭眾謙恭。

translations.literal: Gongren served the Sui with loyalty and honesty, governing the multitude with humility.
translations.idiomatic: Gongren served the Sui with loyal honesty and governed his men with humility.

sentences.zh: 破賊立功，方見仁者有勇；

translations.literal: In breaking the enemy and establishing merit, one then sees that the benevolent have courage.
translations.idiomatic: In defeating the enemy and winning merit, one sees that the benevolent can also be brave.

sentences.zh: 掌選被斥，所謂獨正者危。

translations.literal: In overseeing selection and being driven out, what is called "the one who stands alone in righteousness is in peril."
translations.idiomatic: Yet when he oversaw appointments and was driven out, one saw the truth of the saying that the upright man stands in peril.

sentences.zh: 自偽歸朝，懷才遇主，連婚帝室，列位籓宣，始終無玷者鮮矣！

translations.literal: From submitting after the false regime, holding talent and meeting his lord, marrying into the imperial house, and filling posts as frontier commissioner—the unstained from beginning to end were few!
translations.idiomatic: From surrender after the false Tang through finding favor, marrying into the imperial clan, and holding frontier posts—few remained unstained from start to finish!

sentences.zh: 師道慎密純善，怯懦無更事之名；

translations.literal: Shidao was careful, close-mouthed, and pure in goodness, yet timid and without a name for worldly experience.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao was discreet, honest, and good-hearted, yet timid and without a reputation for practical experience.

sentences.zh: 抑勢避嫌，署用致非才之誚。

translations.literal: In repressing power and avoiding suspicion, his appointments brought the reproach of employing unworthy men.
translations.idiomatic: In curbing influence and avoiding suspicion, his appointments drew criticism for favoring mediocrity.

sentences.zh: 無逸知父守節陷難，離母避逆終吉，忠信之道著矣；

translations.literal: Wuyi knew his father kept integrity and fell into difficulty, left his mother to flee rebellion and in the end was fortunate—the way of loyalty and faith was made clear.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyi honored his father's steadfastness in adversity, left his mother to escape rebellion, and was spared in the end—the path of loyalty and faithfulness was plain.

sentences.zh: 絕賓客以閉府門，斷衣帶以續燈炷，廉介之志彰矣。

translations.literal: In cutting off guests to close the prefectural gate and severing his sash to lengthen a lamp wick, the will to integrity was displayed.
translations.idiomatic: In shutting his gates to visitors and tearing his sash to trim a lamp wick, his incorruptible spirit shone through.

sentences.zh: 於乎，蜀道初開，親老地梗，至孝滅性，子道可知，不得謚為「孝」也，惜哉！

translations.literal: Alas! When the Shu road was first opened, with parents aged and the land obstructed, his utmost filiality destroyed his nature—the son's way is knowable; yet he could not receive the posthumous title "Filial"—a pity!
translations.idiomatic: Alas! When the road to Shu was first opened, with aged parents and the land cut off, his filial devotion cost him his life—the son's duty was clear, yet he could not receive the posthumous title "Filial"—what a pity!

sentences.zh: 大亮文武兼才，貞確成性。

translations.literal: Daliang combined civil and military talent; uprightness and certainty formed his nature.
translations.idiomatic: Daliang united civil and military gifts, and uprightness was the core of his character.

sentences.zh: 賣馬勸農，是為政也；

translations.literal: Selling horses to encourage farming—this was governing.
translations.idiomatic: Selling horses to promote farming—that was good governance.

sentences.zh: 投身諭賊，略也；

translations.literal: Throwing himself in to instruct bandits—this was strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Risking himself to persuade bandits—that was strategic daring.

sentences.zh: 放奴婢從良者，仁也；

translations.literal: Releasing slaves and maidservants to free status—this was benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Freeing slaves and servants to live as commoners—that was benevolence.

sentences.zh: 因鷹諫獵，臨終上表，忠也；

translations.literal: Remonstrating against the hunt through the hawk, submitting a memorial on his deathbed—this was loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating against the hunt by returning a hawk, and submitting a final memorial—that was loyalty.

sentences.zh: 論伊吾之眾，智也；

translations.literal: Discussing the people of Yiwu—this was wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: Counsel on the people of Yiwu—that was wisdom.

sentences.zh: 葬五葉無後，報張弼恩，義也；

translations.literal: Burying five generations without heirs, repaying Zhang Bi's kindness—this was righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Burying childless kinsmen across five generations and repaying Zhang Bi's kindness—that was righteousness.

sentences.zh: 侍兄嫂如父母，孝也；

translations.literal: Serving elder brother and sister-in-law as parents—this was filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Treating his elder brother and sister-in-law as parents—that was filial piety.

sentences.zh: 不死婦人之手，禮也；

translations.literal: Not dying in a woman's hands—this was ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Refusing to die in a woman's hands—that was observance of ritual.

sentences.zh: 無珠玉為唅，廉也。

translations.literal: Having no pearls or jade for the mouth-ceremony—this was integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving no pearls or jade for his burial—that was integrity.

sentences.zh: 房玄齡雲，大亮有王陵、周勃之節，名下無虛士矣！

translations.literal: Fang Xuanling said Daliang had the integrity of Wang Ling and Zhou Bo—in name there was no empty talent!
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling said Daliang had the steadfastness of Wang Ling and Zhou Bo—his reputation was fully deserved!

sentences.zh: 迥秀諂事權幸，爰至台司，余不足觀，清風替矣。

translations.literal: Jiongxiu flattered and served the powerful and favored, thus reaching the high ministerial office—the rest is not worth viewing; the pure wind has fallen away.
translations.idiomatic: Jiongxiu flattered the powerful to reach the highest office—the rest is not worth recounting; a stain upon the age's integrity.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：李綱守道，言行俱危。

translations.literal: In praise: Li Gang kept to the Way; words and deeds alike were perilous.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: Li Gang held to the Way—perilous in word and deed alike.

sentences.zh: 善果母訓，清貞是資。

translations.literal: Shangguo had his mother's instruction; purity and integrity were his resources.
translations.idiomatic: Shangguo drew on his mother's teaching; purity and integrity were his foundation.

sentences.zh: 元璹父子，要道何虧。

translations.literal: Yuanxu, father and son—what essential Way did they lack?
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxu, father and son—what essential virtue did they not betray?

sentences.zh: 恭仁獨正，令德無違。

translations.literal: Gongren stood alone in righteousness; his noble virtue knew no breach.
translations.idiomatic: Gongren stood alone in integrity; his noble conduct never faltered.

sentences.zh: 師道慎密，抑勢見機。

translations.literal: Shidao was careful and close-mouthed; in repressing power he discerned the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao was discreet and cautious; in curbing influence he knew when to act.

sentences.zh: 無逸廉介，終於孝思。

translations.literal: Wuyi was incorruptible and upright, ending in filial remembrance.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyi was incorruptible and upright, and died in filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 大亮才德，陵、勃名隨。

translations.literal: Daliang's talent and virtue—the names of Ling and Bo follow after.
translations.idiomatic: Daliang's talent and virtue—worthy of the names Wang Ling and Zhou Bo.

sentences.zh: 迥秀托附，實污台司。

translations.literal: Jiongxiu leaned on patrons—in truth he stained the high office.
translations.idiomatic: Jiongxiu clung to patrons—in truth he disgraced the highest office.
